articles.title: 华硕上线工作站机箱 PRO WS702：支持 E-ATX 主板，兼容 400mm 扩展卡
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，华硕 (ASUS) 现已在电商平台上线 PRO WS702 机箱。这一型号面向工作站装机，提供 8 条扩展槽，支持 E-ATX 主板，兼容 400mm 扩展卡，标价 999 元但尚未开售。PRO WS702 主体部分三维 248×530×555 (mm)，电源限长 180mm、处理器散热器限高 190mm，提供 4 个 3.5" / 2.5" 盘位、2 个 2.5" 盘位，背部拥有 35mm 理线空间和多处穿线孔与绑线固定点，集成双卡固定支架。该机箱拥有 7 个风扇位，其中前部支持 3 颗 120mm / 140mm 或 2 颗 160mm / 180mm / 200mm 风扇，上部支持 3 颗 120mm / 140mm 风扇，后部支持 1 颗 120mm / 140mm 风扇，前部和上部还兼容 360 / 420 规格冷排；底部配备可拆卸防尘网。其前置 I/O 面板包括 1 个 USB-C 10Gbps、2 个 USB-A 5Gbps、2 个 USB-A 480Mbps、1 个 3.5mm 二合一音频插孔。京东华硕 Pro WS702 机箱 999 元（存疑）直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 全球金融监管标准制定机构呼吁：银行、企业要加强对 AI 智能体的人工监管
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据路透社今天（15 日）午间报道，全球金融监管标准制定机构金融稳定理事会向银行及其他企业发出呼吁，要求加强对 AI 智能体的人工监督，并将这一要求纳入 AI 风险管理的最终版指引。金融稳定理事会公布指引之际，各国监管机构也在加紧防范 AI 带来的风险，其中就包含了利用 AI 发动网络攻击的威胁。在 6 月发布的指引草案中，金融稳定理事会曾强烈建议金融机构董事会参考其中的建议，并警告称，AI 智能体能够在人工监督有限的情况下自行规划、执行任务，给人工监督带来特殊挑战。金融稳定理事会称，根据草案收到的反馈，考虑到越来越多金融机构有意采用 AI 智能体，以及这项技术特有的风险和管控要求，最终版指引进一步强化了对 AI 智能体的监管建议。一系列事件加深了政策制定者的担忧，AI 系统有能力绕过安全防护措施。据IT之家了解，今年 7 月，一个 OpenAI 智能体就曾脱离受控测试环境，并入侵 AI 公司 Hugging Face。根据修订后的指引，对于风险较高的 AI 应用，加强人工监督至关重要。企业还应根据风险程度明确规定，AI 智能体在什么情况下必须先获得人工批准，才能继续执行任务。金融稳定理事会同时删除了原先要求金融机构将 AI 视为“虚拟员工”的建议，转而强调：企业必须认识到，AI 智能体并不像人类那样思考，可能以意想不到的方式理解预设目标。相关阅读：《联合国秘书长古特雷斯呼吁全球监管人工智能，避免出现杀人机器人》

articles.title: 2026 年 9 月国内动力电池装车量 87.2GWh，同比增长 14.7%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，中国汽车动力电池产业创新联盟今日发布了 2026 年 9 月动力电池月度信息。产量方面：9 月，我国动力和储能电池合计产量为 237.8GWh，环比增长 0.3%，同比增长 57.3%。1-9 月，我国动力和储能电池累计产量为 1833.1GWh，累计同比增长 63.4%。销量方面：9 月，我国动力和储能电池销量为 222.7GWh，环比下降 0.2%，同比增长 52.0%。其中，动力电池销量为 149.2GWh，占总销量 67.0%，环比增长 1.7%，同比增长 35.0%；储能电池销量为 73.5GWh，占总销量 33.0%，环比下降 3.7%，同比增长 104.4%。1-9 月，我国动力和储能电池累计销量为 1681.7GWh，累计同比增长 57.6%。其中，动力电池累计销量为 1086.4GWh，占总销量 64.6%，累计同比增长 38.2%；储能电池累计销量为 595.4GWh，占总销量 35.4%，累计同比增长 111.8%。9 月，我国动力和储能电池合计出口 44.0GWh，环比增长 3.7%，同比增长 64.5%，占当月销量 19.7%。其中，动力电池出口量为 28.4GWh，占总出口量 64.5%，环比增长 14.9%，同比增长 60.9%；储能电池出口量为 15.6GWh，占总出口量 35.5%，环比下降 11.9%，同比增长 71.4%。1-9 月，我国动力和储能电池累计出口 302.9GWh，累计同比增长 51.6%，占累计销量 18.0%。其中，动力电池累计出口为 199.7GWh，占总出口量 65.9%，累计同比增长 54.7%；储能电池累计出口量为 103.2GWh，占总出口量 34.1%，累计同比增长 45.9%。装车量方面：9 月，国内动力电池装车量 87.2GWh，环比增长 10.4%，同比增长 14.7%。其中三元电池装车量 12.3GWh，占总装车量 14.1%，环比增长 11.7%，同比下降 10.9%；磷酸铁锂电池装车量 74.5GWh，占总装车量 85.5%，环比增长 10.3%，同比增长 19.9%。1-9 月，国内动力电池累计装车量 576.3GWh，累计同比增长 16.7%。其中三元电池累计装车量 97.9GWh，占总装车量 17.0%，累计同比增长 7.3%；磷酸铁锂电池累计装车量 477.2GWh，占总装车量 82.8%，累计同比增长 18.5%。IT之家注意到，宁德时代以 35.49GWh、40.92% 的份额继续居首，但占比较上月回落 0.52 个百分点；比亚迪装车量 18.29GWh、份额 21.09%，环比微升 0.11 个百分点，两家合计份额仍超六成。

articles.title: Molavi: Saudis & Houthis Can Hit Hard; Not End War
articles.content: Oil prices were low as concerns eased in the Middle East over supply disruptions. This is after the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia did not cause any interruptions that markets had feared. The IEA also raised its forecast for the war's impact on supply. Meanwhile the question looms of US military support to Saudi Arabia in their fight against the Iran-backed rebels in Yemen. Afshin Molavi, senior fellow at Johns Hopkins University's School of Advanced International Studies spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa on the likelihood of US involvement. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，型号为“iPhone19,4”的苹果手机昨日（10 月 14 日）现身 GeekBench 跑分库，目前显示关于 CPU、GPU 和 AI 的多条跑分记录。基于苹果型号列表等信息，该手机关联苹果首款折叠 iPhone Duo。在 GeekBench 跑分平台上，目前 iPhone Duo 在 GeekBench 7 CPU 中共有 6 条记录，在 GeekBench 7 GPU 中共有 3 条记录，在 GeekBench AI 中有 1 条记录。从跑分成绩来看，和 iPhone 18 Pro 系列的差别并不大。在 CPU 跑分方面，这里附上多核跑分最高的一条记录，显示单核成绩为 3,985 分，多核成绩为 11,271 分。Geekbench 信息显示，iPhone Duo 的 6 核 CPU 基础频率为 4.93GHz，与 iPhone 18 Pro 跑分中的频率一致。该机显示 11.30GB 内存，对应 12GB 运行内存。IT之家附上相关图片如下：在 GPU 方面，共有 3 条记录，目前最高分为 61,531 分。在 AI 性能方面，iPhone Duo 的单精度成绩为 6,845 分，半精度成绩为 12,109 分，量化成绩为 9,076 分。相关阅读：《A20 Pro 芯片 AI 跑分曝光：苹果 iPhone 18 Pro NPU 较前代最高增幅 51.53%》《A20 Pro 跑分首曝：苹果 iPhone 18 Pro Max 现身 Geekbench，搭载 12GB 内存》

articles.title: 三星电子首席设计官波尔奇尼：AI 时代，人的创造力才是产品设计核心竞争力
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据韩媒 ETnews 报道，三星电子设备体验（DX）事业部总裁兼首席设计官毛罗 · 波尔奇尼称，三星坚持以人为本的设计理念，将 AI 与人的情感智能、想象力相结合。波尔奇尼今天（15 日）在“2026 首尔设计周”上指出：“AI 不是用来取代人的，而是帮助人们发挥情感智能和想象力的工具。只有将 AI 与人的创造本能和欲望相结合，才能真正创造出独特的价值。越是在 AI 时代，人的因素反而越重要。人类独有的批判性思维、创造力、感受力和情感，才是产品设计的核心。”波尔奇尼强调，无论 AI 技术如何进步，设计的根本仍然是理解人的需求。如果所有企业都只依靠 AI 开发产品，最终生产出来的东西就会大同小异，难以形成差异化。因此，人的创造力和细腻的感受力将成为产品设计的核心竞争力。三星电子将这一理念贯穿电视、智能手机、家电等产品的设计。除了提升硬件性能，三星还希望通过体现用户生活方式和个性的设计，让产品形成差异化。“技术应该帮助用户提高效率，让人们有更多闲暇时间，同时发挥人的潜能，帮助人们留住生活中的珍贵时刻。我们会继续推出造福人类、改善生活的设计。”IT之家获悉，波尔奇尼是国际知名设计师，曾担任 3M 和百事公司的首席设计官。2025 年 4 月，他加入三星电子担任首席设计官，统筹设备体验事业部的产品设计工作。

articles.title: 微软办公 AI 智能体技术突破：不换模型响应提速 400%，词元消耗减 30%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，科技媒体 NeoWin 今天（10 月 15 日）发布博文，报道称在企业内部知识密集型场景下，微软为 Copilot 等 AI 智能体带来技术突破，不升级底层大模型的前提下，AI 智能体响应速度提升至原来的 4 倍，同时词元（Token）消耗减少约 30%。IT之家援引博文介绍，微软表示在企业办公场景中，项目信息往往零散分布于邮件、Teams 会议记录和技术文档中。以往 AI 智能体需要逐一检索并处理这些碎片化源数据，导致高延迟与高昂的计算成本。而最新技术依托于 SharePoint 并搭载了微软全新的 Work IQ 知识编译引擎，能够自动转化跨组织机构的散落信息为结构化知识库，供 AI 智能体直接、高效地调取。在适用场景方面，主要覆盖跨文档问答、团队上下文检索，整理会议要点、汇总项目状态、检索内部流程、准备客户沟通材料，或按既有资料生成初稿等。该功能现已向 Frontier Preview 租户推出。组织可将知识库添加至现有 SharePoint 网站，包括支撑 Teams 频道和 Microsoft 365 群组的网站。该预览功能目前仅向启用按使用量计费的用户开放，管理员可通过 Microsoft 365 管理中心管理访问权限与支出。微软还计划扩展至 Copilot Studio 自定义智能体，并开发自动化维护能力，让知识库随企业内容更新。

articles.title: Show HN: Real Design Benchmark – can you tell AI designs from real products?
articles.content: Hi HN,I'm Adam Ginzberg, one of the cofounders of Subframe, a code-first design tool.One of the things I'm really curious about is understanding LLM performance on subjective domains like design.As an experiment I built this game which presents two designs of the same screen, one of which was generated by AI. First you pick which one you like better and then which one you think was made by AI.Most design work happens in an existing product, so we set up this game to test that. As context, the AI gets 4 screenshots from the existing product, the product's icons + fonts, and a written brief about the screen it is asked to build. It then writes HTML which is screenshotted identically to the real screen. To get the data, we signed up for the products with test accounts and added dummy data. All of the inputs were manually checked to make sure nothing about the target screen was leaked in the prompt. You can read more about the methodology at https://www.realdesignbenchmark.com/methodology.

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，尼康 Z 5II C 全画幅微单相机于今日正式发售，黑色机身（不含镜头）售价为 9999 元。该机定位新手入门，主打随手出片轻松拍，目前可叠加平台满 6000-780 元神券，券后 9219 元。京东尼康（Nikon）Z5IIC 全画幅微单相机 黑色机身 (不含镜头) 券后 9219 元领 780 元券Z5ⅡC 机身（黑色 / 银色）：RMB 9,999 元Z5ⅡC（黑色 / 银色）+ 尼克尔 Z 24-50mm f/4-6.3 套机：RMB 11,999 元Z5ⅡC（黑色 / 银色）+ 尼克尔 Z 24-105mm f/4-7.1 套机：RMB 12,799 元Z5ⅡC（黑色 / 银色）+ 尼克尔 Z 24-200mm f/4-6.3 VR 套机：RMB 15,499 元其机身重 620 克，采用镁合金，提供银色和黑色两种配色，具备防尘防溅设计，使用轻巧便携、利于收纳的平顶设计和握持感稳固舒适的手柄。Z5IIC 配备 24.5MP 全画幅背照式 CMOS 传感器与 EXPEED 7 图像处理器，支持 10 种类型的对象侦测，具有精准快速的自动对焦性能、最低达-10EV 的暗光对焦表现和最高约 1 秒的预拍功能。尼康首次在全画幅无反中加入场景模式，共 15 种选项，覆盖人像、宠物、食物、夜景和黄昏等，还有自动调整拍摄参数的 AUTO 模式；支持五轴机身防抖，可提供最高 7.5 档补偿；还有胶片颗粒功能，可调整颗粒大小和强度。用户选定场景后，相机自动优化色彩、亮度、白平衡和优化校准等设置。机身还设有专用按钮，可快速调用成像配方。自动对焦基于深度学习，可检测并追踪人、狗、猫、鸟、车辆、飞机和鱼，支持眼部锁定。AUTO 模式会分析主体和场景，自动优化对焦、光圈、快门和 ISO。这款新机还支持连接尼康云创和 SnapBridge，机身上专用的优化校准按钮可快速切换色彩方案，引入胶片颗粒功能，轻松打造个性化的影像风格。该机采用 3.2 英寸可变角度监视器，可翻转用于自拍和 Vlog；连拍速度最高约 14fps，高速帧捕获 + 模式下可达 30fps，并支持预拍摄，记录快门释放前最多 1 秒；视频支持 4K UHD 60fps、Full HD 120fps，以及 4 倍和 5 倍慢动作。视频方面，该机还支持 H.265 10-bit MOV、N-Log 和 N-RAW 录制至 SD 卡。通过 USB 连接 PC，可使用 UVC / UAC 进行直播。尼康称，Z5IIC 的“C”代表 casual，即休闲，旨在通过直观控制和自动化功能降低全画幅使用门槛。IT之家附详细参数如下：京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: 比尔 · 盖茨认为 AI 比核武器更危险、比核能更有用，与 PC、互联网等创新都不同
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据 Vatican News 本周报道，微软创始人比尔 · 盖茨谈到了 AI 增长可能带来的危险，并解释说 AI 是一个无法自我监管的领域，因此必须由政府引导，必须采取行动，利用 AI 在医疗、教育和农业领域所带来的机遇。比尔 · 盖茨表示，我们没有足够关注 AI 的风险，也没有尽量减少伤害。我们也没有做足够的工作来充分利用当前的 AI 机遇，AI 可以让农村医生将智能手机当作超声波机器使用，为学生根据实际学习方式进行个性化辅导，并根据农民的土壤和气候提供量身定制的建议。他表示，这些都不是自动发生的，如果任由市场发展，最强大的工具会优先被付钱最多的人使用，而不是最需要的人。“这就是为什么我们在未来两年内承诺投入十亿美元，推动 AI 在市场力量最后达到的健康、教育和农业领域使用。风险和机遇以相同的速度前进，我们必须同时对两者采取行动。”比尔 · 盖茨还表示，AI 与人类以往见过的任何技术都不同。过去像个人电脑或互联网这样的创新，这一模式最初是经历了重大颠覆，但最终会奏效，人们最终拥有更好的工具。AI 不同，它更像是一个进化事件，我们创造了一种在许多方面与人类认知相当甚至超越人类的智能。把它当作“下一台个人电脑”来看待，会让人们完全低估它。比尔 · 盖茨认为可以把 AI 分成两个不同的时期。目前，我们正处于一个转型期，虽然还没有在各方面都拥有大规模的积极性，但确实带来了真正的颠覆。在这一时期需要多方面的改变，包括如何对待劳动力与税收，我们有意为人类保留哪些岗位，以及如何确保技术真正惠及最能受益的人，而不仅仅是那些能拿出最多钱的人。等到转型结束，如果我们把护栏和通行权安排妥当，我们就能看到一个真正丰盛的世界：AI 和人形机器人能够处理食物、住所和其他基本生活所需，那个时期将引发关于意义和人们如何消磨时间这种完全不同的问题。比尔 · 盖茨表示，现在的重点是让人类度过接下来的几年，避免发生灾难性的生物恐怖袭击或网络安全事件，也不让大量就业市场或世界大片地区被抛下。比尔 · 盖茨还认为 AI 是一种比核武器更危险的技术，且可能比核能更有益。他认为增加基本的安全检查几乎不会减缓 AI 发展速度，而且能够大大降低风险，这是值得做的交易。他担心的是，可能要等到严重的网络攻击或严重的生物恐怖事件发生后，各国政府才会真正重视这件事。另据 CNN 报道，比尔 · 盖茨预测，AI 技术的快速发展将在 2027 年带来众多网络安全威胁，他认为 AI 驱动的网络攻击将是明年经历最重大变化的领域之一。不过他也表示，AI 失控还不是人类最紧迫的问题。他说，这项技术还需要几年的发展，才能对世界产生大规模影响。

articles.title: 苹果“春晚”后首场顶级实战：iPhone 18 Pro Max 挑大梁掌镜土耳其时装秀
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，苹果公司昨日（10 月 14 日）发布公告，宣布携手潮牌 Les Benjamins，在土耳其卡帕多奇亚（Cappadocia）的玫瑰谷（Rose Valley）上演名为“From Earth to Sky”（从大地到天空）的时装秀。IT之家注：Les Benjamins 成立于 2011 年，由设计师 Bünyamin Aydın 创立，起初以印花 T 恤起家，如今已发展为涵盖男装、女装、卫衣、运动套装、外套、牛仔及生活方式产品的品牌。本次时装秀也是为了庆祝该品牌成立 15 周年。在本次时装秀期间，最亮眼的是 3 个翱翔于峡谷上空的巨型热气球，由 Aydın 借助 iPad Pro 搭配 Apple Pencil Pro 在 Procreate 软件中绘制完成的。Aydın 透露，Apple Pencil Pro 的“悬停预览”（Hover）功能就像一件“超自然工具”，让他能在落笔前规避错误，完美将安纳托利亚的本地花卉转化为巨型飞行艺术装置的技术图纸。除了通过 iPad 设计巨型热气球外，苹果公司还表示在本次活动中，全程使用 iPhone 18 Pro Max 拍摄记录。法国知名导演 Neels Castillon 全程使用 iPhone 18 Pro Max 掌镜记录了整场大秀，海外科技媒体称这是苹果秋季发布会（国内数码爱好者戏称为苹果科技春晚）后，iPhone 18 Pro Max 的首场顶级实战。得益于 iPhone 18 Pro Max 的可变光圈技术与强劲的 A20 Pro 芯片，摄制组在日光剧烈变化的环境下实现了平滑的画面过渡，并利用特制无人机搭载手机，完成了 4K 120fps ProRes RAW 的高难度电影级慢动作航拍。以上图源：苹果

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，漫步者 NeoBuds Pro 5 30 周年典藏版现已上架，定价为 1169 元。这款耳机是漫步者 30 周年纪念典藏版本，全球限量发行 3000 套，每台耳机带有独立编号，随箱附赠徽章和纪念卡。京东漫步者（EDIFIER）NeoBuds Pro 5 30 周年典藏版券后 1110.55 元领 0.95 元券声学架构方面，这款耳机升级为 1 圈 2 铁三分频配置，采用 1 个高分子振膜动圈单元加 2 个楼氏动铁单元，搭配三分频技术。其中楼氏双动铁负责高频和超高频表现，高分子大尺寸宽声场动圈包揽中低频，可还原录音室原始的声音细节，带来监听级音质享受。音质方面，该耳机支持 LHDC 192 / LDAC 编码，实现 192kHz / 24bit 高清采样，并且获得了 Hi-Res Wireless 和 HWA 双金标认证。这款耳机搭载带有头部追踪的杜比全景声音效，实现声随头动，立体音效始终环绕四周，号称听歌观影都可以带来沉浸式的 VIP 包厢体验。降噪方面，它采用漫步者 EDIFIER WIDE-BAND MULTI-CHANNEL ANC 专利降噪技术，支持宽频自适应降噪，可实现 -53dB 降噪深度、 5kHz 降噪宽度，能智能识别环境并自动调整降噪参数。其配备 3 麦 + 骨导 + AI 降噪方案，在地铁、街头、风雨中也可以精准滤除环境噪音，保证对方能听到清晰的人声，甚至可以应对 32km/h 风速骑行场景。其综合续航可达 46 小时：降噪关闭时耳机续航约 10 小时，充电盒补充后总计约 46 小时；降噪开启时耳机续航约 5.5 小时，充电盒补充后总计约 25 小时，同时支持快充，快充 15 分钟即可续航约 3.5 小时。IT之家附详细参数如下：京东 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 3 次：点此抽红包。淘宝 11.11 无门槛红包 面额至高 26888 元，每天抽 1 次：点此抽红包。

articles.title: IDC：2026 年三季度全球智能手机出货量同比暴跌 22%，为史上最严重季度下滑
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据彭博社报道，市场研究机构 IDC 表示，受内存涨价冲击，全球智能手机市场在今年第三季度遭遇史上最严重季度下滑，出货量同比大跌 22%，降至 2.553 亿台，后续形势还会进一步恶化。IDC 称，过去一年，人工智能行业订单拉动存储芯片价格走高，挤压整个手机行业的利润空间，迫使厂商上调售价、缩减硬件配置，甚至砍掉入门机型。小米、OPPO 等中国头部品牌受到的冲击最为严重；苹果与三星电子凭借更丰富的高端机型矩阵，表现相对更好。IT之家注意到，设备厂商越来越意识到，行业正在经历永久性结构性转变。IDC 预测，市场增长至少要等到 2028 年才有可能复苏。随着厂商持续涨价、引导消费者选购旗舰或超高端机型，长期趋势会是：市场整体盘子缩小，但苹果这类拥有庞大渠道与高端产品组合的厂商，所占市场份额会进一步提升。IDC 研究总监纳比拉 · 波帕尔（Nabila Popal）表示：“当前各项指标显示市场尚未触底。内存价格自去年以来暴涨约 350%，而且仍在继续上涨，给厂商的利润和出货量带来巨大压力。最艰难的阶段还在后面。”

articles.title: Anthropic 国际业务负责人普兰森：开放式 AI 模型比我们的模型风险更高
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据彭博社 14 日报道，Anthropic 国际业务负责人、负责美国以外市场销售的纪尧姆 · 普兰森认为，与 Anthropic 自家的 AI 模型相比，开放式模型发生网络安全事件或造成其他危害的风险更高。普兰森在都柏林国际人工智能峰会期间接受采访时表示：“对开源模型的安全问题，我们必须格外小心。我无法替开放模型作出保证，但从定义上讲，这类模型的风险更高。”随着越来越多国家担心过度依赖美国 AI 技术，预计将上市的 Anthropic 面临越来越激烈的竞争。其中，开放权重 AI 模型成为热门选择。IT之家注：开放权重 AI 模型向公众开放参数，用户可以自行修改，也能部署在自己的设备上。支持者认为，开放权重模型比 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 严格控制的闭源模型更便宜，也更有利于各国掌握 AI 技术自主权。Anthropic 还进一步加强了对 AI 潜在风险的警告。本周早些时候，公司警告称，小型 AI 模型很快就可能被用来驱动新型僵尸网络，使其能够在智能烤箱等小型联网设备之间自行复制和扩散。普兰森还负责 Anthropic 面向初创企业和数字原生企业的销售业务。他称，对开放权重模型的担忧来自 Anthropic 保护自家产品安全的经验。在几起引发广泛关注的 AI 黑客攻击事件后，Anthropic 宣称增加了安全防护措施，防止模型从事恶意活动。Anthropic 也一直主张，在国际标准和统一的评估机制建立之前，应该放慢 AI 开发步伐。普兰森还谈到了公司定价较高的模型。他经常告诉企业，购买能力更强的模型最终是值得的。“应该持续投资最先进的模型，因为无论是半年、一年还是两年后，同样的应用成本都会下降。”普兰森称，Anthropic 最新推出的 Claude Opus 5.5 模型比早期版本便宜 40%。付费使用 Anthropic 前沿模型的企业客户占公司业务的“很大一部分”，但他没有透露具体比例。

articles.title: OpenAI 伦敦分部去年人均薪酬超 230 万英镑，堪比英超球星
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 15 日消息，据卫报报道，OpenAI 伦敦分部员工去年人均薪酬达到 231.8181 万英镑（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,053.9 万元人民币）。这家 ChatGPT 开发商投入堪比英超球星级别的薪资，全力争夺全球 AI 竞赛的主导地位。OpenAI 英国有限公司注册于威斯敏斯特，新总部落地伦敦国王十字区。公司财报显示，110 名员工合计领取 8,700 万英镑（现汇率约合 7.71 亿元人民币）薪资，外加价值 1.68 亿英镑（现汇率约合 14.88 亿元人民币）的公司股权。OpenAI 目标上市估值约 1 万亿美元（现汇率约合 6.71 万亿元人民币）。英国国家统计局数据显示，这份平均薪酬是英国全职员工收入中位数的 58 倍。拿到平均薪酬包的 OpenAI 员工，税前时薪（薪资 + 股权）约 1,000 英镑（现汇率约合 8,860 元人民币）。不过内部薪酬差距巨大，最高档薪酬留给 AI 研究员，正是他们打造出这家旧金山企业 Astra 等前沿大模型。数据对应的是 2025 年，彼时行业人才争夺战白热化，其竞争对手 Meta 当时传出提供数亿美元的多年期人才包。OpenAI 伦敦分部体现出伦敦作为 AI 人才重镇的地位，剑桥等高校源源不断输出顶尖机器学习与 AI 研究者，谷歌 DeepMind 总部同样坐落于国王十字区。今年夏天，正在训练阶段的 OpenAI AI 智能体发生逃逸，入侵了无关网站 Hugging Face；本月，OpenAI 一名安全负责人离职，称企业文化已经崩坏，各大 AI 企业在技术研发上“谨慎程度远远不够”。OpenAI 伦敦办公室是其规模最大的海外研发中心，同时设有政府事务、销售与市场团队，负责向各类企业与机构出售授权。英国前保守党财政大臣乔治 · 奥斯本于去年 12 月入职，担任该公司国别事务负责人。相比上一年人均 110 万英镑（现汇率约合 974.6 万元人民币）的薪酬 + 股权包，本次收入水平大幅上涨。AI 行业高薪浪潮已经显著推高旧金山房价：当地一居室公寓租金均值达到每月 4,400 美元（现汇率约合 29,509 元人民币），同比上涨超 25%，接近美国平均水平的三倍。房东们借着 AI 热潮获利，尤其是 OpenAI、Anthropic 这类头部 AI 企业办公地点周边的房源。在伦敦，OpenAI 英国有限公司 2025 年营收增长两倍多，达到 2.93 亿英镑（现汇率约合 25.96 亿元人民币），实现利润 2,030 万英镑（现汇率约合 1.8 亿元人民币）。

articles.content:

Abstract: Under the accelerated pace of AI development, any benchmark whose difficulty is calibrated with humans or current AI systems becomes circular, or saturates soon. How can we then evaluate machines that may become more capable than the current machines and the people who write the tests? One answer to the question hinges on inverse problems, inductive inference questions for which difficulty depends on the complexity of the underlying mechanism, given the observations and the previous knowledge. Levin's Kt, a computable variant of Kolmogorov complexity, puts a theoretical upper bound to that difficulty, balancing the simplest representation encoding for the mechanism and the logarithm of the time steps to run that mechanism. Previous tests derived from Levin's Kt, such as the original C-test, are based on minimalistic Universal Turing Machines (UTM), capable of very limited representations and no previous knowledge. articles.title: The Silent Failures in Agentic Data Science
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14115v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models have significantly lowered the barrier to writing code. Naturally, this has also led to the development of data science agents that promise automating the design and execution of data science from task formulation to model development. Existing evaluations of agentic data science (agentic DS) assess downstream predictive performance and code correctness, providing preliminary insight in agentic DS capabilities. We argue that these evaluations overlook the fundamental principles of data science: methodological data science- and domain knowledge. As such, only assessing downstream performance masks methodological failures such as data leakage and inappropriate validation, limiting the development of robust agentic DS systems. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14118v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven their deployment toward general-purpose harness environments, where LLM-based agents operate in sandbox workspaces and interact directly with file systems and shells. While numerous post-training pipelines exist for tool-use agents, their counterparts for harness-based agents remain scarce and are predominantly one-shot and teacher-dependent: a stronger external model synthesizes tasks and collects trajectories, the target agent is trained once, and evaluation results are consumed by human researchers rather than fed back into the loop. Such pipelines are inherently bounded by the capability of the external model and the scope of human prior, leaving no room for self-improvement. articles.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14136v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Iterative sampling in diffusion models can lead to error accumulation due to exposure bias. The denoiser is trained on real images interpolated with noise, but at inference its inputs are constructed from its own imperfect predictions from the earlier steps, something it has never seen at training time. This might be one reason diffusion models often struggle without additional help, such as CFG. We introduce a correction step for diffusion models which attempts to reduce this training-inference gap. The corrector takes the base model's prediction as input and is trained against the same ground-truth target. This makes correction an explicit learning task, with training inputs provided by the base model. During sampling, at each denoising step, we iteratively refine the denoiser's clean-sample prediction. Abstract: Long-horizon terminal benchmarks measure whether an agent can sustain progress through extended workflows with process rewards, not only whether its final state passes a binary check. articles.title: Unconstrained CTI-REALM with Open-Weights
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14180v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Organisations that want language-model agents for security work face a choice between open-weight models, which they can run and audit themselves, and far more expensive closed frontier models. We study that choice on CTI-REALM (arXiv:2603.13517), a benchmark in which an agent turns a threat-intelligence report into a working detection by querying a live telemetry store. We evaluate twenty-six models, nineteen open-weight and seven closed, under a common harness, scorer and panel of LLM judges. Our main finding is that an open-weight model can match the strongest closed models at less than a tenth of their cost, provided it is given enough turns. articles.title: Visualizing the World Model in an Agent's Value Function
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14186v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Could model-free reinforcement learning algorithms actually be learning a model of the environment? In this work, we apply counterfactual interventions which hold everything about a state fixed, besides a targeted change, to explore if the value function of a Proximal Policy Optimization agent forms a world model of the Crafter environment. Despite only being trained to optimize reward, we discover that the value function learns concepts such as the rules governing when a diamond is collectible, water and food having an impact on health, heuristics regarding inventory, and more. Finally, we discuss the safety implications of our visualizations and some shortcomings of current reinforcement learning agents that will prevent us from building truly advanced machine intelligence.

Abstract: The most accurate agents executing user-provided tasks are driven by large, cloud-hosted models, which solve them by reading the private data of the user. Agents powered by models small enough to run on edge devices keep that data local, but yield far worse results. A third option is to have cloud models write a program that devices execute: the data stays local, but as the program is written before any data is seen, it fails whenever a step depends on interpreting content that appears only at run time. We explore an intermediate architecture, in which the cloud-written program defers bounded questions over user data to a small local model through an ordinary function call. On AppWorld this improves the success rate of a code-only agent in all six combinations of backbone model and test partition we evaluate, by up to 14.9pp, recovering a substantial part of the gap to a cloud-hosted ReAct loop while keeping user data on the device.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14224v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising approach to automatically evolve these harnesses. However, deploying RSI in open-world settings still faces two critical challenges. First, open-world tasks are typically unseen during the harness design phase and novel at test time, leaving no ground-truth verifiers to reliably guide online harness edits. Second, the RSI process remains highly task-specific and fails to generalize to novel scenarios. We introduce Harness^2, a plug-and-play, recursive agent harnessing framework that addresses these challenges through two connected levels of recursion. Task-level recursion refines the current task's harness using a contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose step that reliably guides edits without ground-truth verifiers, and can be scaled further via parallel or sequential recursion. articles.title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14277v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. Sending 4-bit instead of 16-bit values would cut this cost by nearly 4x, but the all-reduce must add the values it carries, and rounding the sum injects an error at every call. Model quality depends on how these errors accumulate over layers, yet existing methods treat each call on its own. We present Echo, a 4-bit all-reduce for training and inference that controls the accumulated error. Echo moves data in 4 bits and sums in high precision, so each value is quantized at most twice per call for any number of GPUs. The summation reveals each injected error, and Echo feeds it back into later calls, so old errors cancel instead of accumulating. articles.title: Controllable Diverse Sampling through Pullback Directions
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14294v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conditional diffusion models can generate high-quality images that align closely with a given prompt. However, samples generated from different random seeds may remain visually similar, limiting creative exploration. Existing approaches can increase variation, but often require additional optimization or sampling overhead, while stronger perturbations may introduce distortions that degrade image quality or prompt alignment. We propose a training-free method that leverages the local pullback geometry induced by the mapping from the conditioning-embedding space to the image space to identify directions of maximal output sensitivity. By steering different sampling trajectories along these directions, we encourage distinct generations while maintaining consistency with the conditioning signal. Experiments on MS-COCO and BrushNet show the efficacy of the method in improving diversity on prompt-conditioned image generation and inpainting.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14307v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose ConicFlow, which frames constrained sampling from a flow matching model at inference time as an optimal control problem that balances deviation from the pretrained trajectory against reward, subject to hard terminal constraints. We discretize this problem and adapt receding-horizon control, optimizing only a short window of the trajectory at each step for computational tractability. We address the resulting sequence of receding-horizon subproblems with a receding-horizon primal-dual algorithm. Its dual multipliers capture the difficulty of satisfying each constraint and are refined throughout sampling, steering generation toward feasible final samples. We further propose a terminal-estimate variant that avoids accumulating local truncation errors by evaluating the reward and constraints at the predicted terminal point rather than at the end of the current horizon. articles.content:

Abstract: In Model Context Protocol (MCP) systems, LLMs select tools from metadata rather than from their implementations. Names and descriptions summarize what a tool does, while the parameter schema specifies the fields a tool accepts and how they are organized. Our analysis of metadata for 367,174 MCP tools reveals substantial schema variation among functionally similar tools. Many of these tools share names and similar descriptions but expose different parameter schemas. We study this question through controlled metadata interventions across five LLMs and five tasks. Abstract: AI-enabled systems must remain dependable when the conditions under which they operate change (e.g., due to input perturbations, distribution shifts, or changes in external dependencies). articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14360v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) alignment often assumes that the user interacting with a model is also the primary beneficiary of its behavior. Yet in many consequential settings, one person directs the system while another bears the consequences. We study this problem in caregiver-mediated healthcare, where parents, pet owners, and caregivers make decisions for children, animals, and older adults. We introduce an evidence-grounded benchmark spanning veterinary, pediatric, and older-adult care, and test whether AI advisors maintain appropriate care when users express clinically inferior preferences. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14381v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as scientific assistants, yet we still lack reliable ways to evaluate whether they can investigate a system rather than merely answer a prompt. A useful evaluation must let agents choose experiments, interpret finite evidence, and make causal decisions, while keeping the environment coherent across repeated observations and interventions and preserving objective ground truth. We introduce ACED-BENCH (Active Causal Evidence and Decision Benchmark), a neuro-symbolic benchmark built around this requirement. The key idea is to separate the readable scientific surface from the formal causal world: LLMs generate natural-language scenarios and task text, while hidden probabilistic graphical models define the causal graph, data-generating process, intervention semantics, validation checks, and oracle answers. Abstract: Agentic AI systems operating over geospatial data require more than autonomous reasoning and tool use; they must also support explicit orchestration, spatial validation, governance, provenance, failure handling, and human decision authority. articles.title: Measuring the Inference Energy Efficiency of Open-Weight LLMs across Benchmarks, Reasoning Modes, and Hardware
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14389v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Benchmark scores tell us what an LLM can do, but not how much energy is required to deliver that capability. We directly measure this trade-off for 86 open-weight model checkpoints, evaluated on seven benchmarks and six hardware platforms ranging from a consumer GPU to an eight-GPU server. We find large differences in energy efficiency even among models with similar capability. Most configurations lie away from the score--energy Pareto frontier: they use a median of 2.6--4.8$\times$ more energy than another configuration that scores at least as well, with differences reaching 27$\times$. Reasoning can improve capability, but enabling thinking increases energy by about 3.7$\times$ on average, and the benefit depends strongly on the model family and output budget. arXiv:2610.18877v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series language models typically align numerical signals with language using labels, captions, or question-answer pairs. Although such supervision encourages linguistic representations, it does not explicitly require them to preserve information about how the underlying time-series signal evolves. We introduce forecast grounding, a pretraining principle that requires language-aligned time-series representations to remain predictive of the future evolution before they are adapted to downstream tasks. We instantiate this principle in LOTUS, which divides each time-series channel into non-overlapping patches and maps them into the LLM embedding space. Abstract: Post-training reasoning LLMs often requires making a tradeoff between costly supervision and compute inefficiency: supervised finetuning typically requires reasoning traces, which is data inefficient since in many applications one only has prompt-answer tuples and lacks the groundtruth chain-of-thought (CoT) sequence. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.18880v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-throughput perturbation screens increasingly use machine-learning models to predict the effects of gene combinations that were never measured. A difficult case arises when both genes in a test pair were seen individually during training, but their combination was not. In this setting, standard OOD methods often fail because neither gene appears unfamiliar on its own. We therefore compare each model prediction with a simple additive prediction obtained by summing the two observed single-gene effects. The difference between them, which we call additive disagreement (AD), measures how much extra interaction effect the model introduces for an unseen combination. Abstract: Token-selection methods for on-policy distillation (OPD) prioritize student-visited positions using diverse signals, including uncertainty, teacher-student disagreement, and mismatch direction. Abstract: Current scaling law formulations suggest that increasing the number of unique samples in a dataset improves model performance, while repeated exposure to the same samples provides diminishing value. Abstract: Real measurements are too limited to train an accurate indoor pathloss predictor that works across a wide range of buildings. Large-scale synthetic pretraining offers a way forward, but real building layouts are also scarce, and accurate ray-tracing simulators are slow, expensive, and often proprietary. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19038v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study online task assignment with reusable resources. This problem arises in peer reviewer assignment, skill-based call routing, rideshare matching, emergency dispatch, and crowdsourcing: Tasks arrive according to a geometric process and must be immediately assigned to servers that become temporarily busy, yielding rewards that depend on the task-server pair. From its dual we obtain Lag, a closed-form index policy. We introduce a scaling regime in which the number of copies of each server and the number of arrivals per step grow together. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19046v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Information-theoretic exploration is of primary interest in methodological studies of reinforcement learning (RL) and computational cognitive neuroscience, while the established RL theory builds regret guarantees on confidence sets. This situation leaves open the conditions under which the information-driven exploration found in nature is more advantageous than the exploration of the established RL theory. We put the state-of-the-art methods of these two paradigms, Active Inference (AIF) and Bayes-UCBVI, on an equal footing: both act through the same state abstraction of a tabular MDP with $S$ states, and their greedy forms differ only in the exploration term. We find that AIF's information gain decays too fast to serve as a confidence width, locking greedy agents that explore by it out of the optimal action. arXiv:2610.19053v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Inference of phylogenetic trees from sequences plays a central role in understanding evolutionary relationships, with applications ranging from tracking pathogen spread to reconstructing the history of life. Conventionally, practitioners obtain posteriors over trees using likelihood-based methods like MCMC. However, likelihoods are only available for simple evolutionary models with restrictive assumptions. For realistic evolutionary models, inference using conventional methods is prohibitively expensive, inaccurate, or even impossible. In practice, practitioners settle for using as flexible a conventional method as possible, even though they expect it is misspecified. In principle, we could use simulation-based inference: simulate tree and sequence data from an evolutionary model and train a neural network to predict the posterior over trees given sequences. Abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) across geographically distributed and poorly interconnected compute pools or data centers has become a topic of significant interest. This has led to increased study of local optimization methods such as DiLoco for LLMs, especially those that use local (or inner) adaptive or preconditioned optimizers, which are critical for high-performance LLM training. However, a central challenge remains: it is well known that increasing the number of model replicas (replica scaling) while fixing the total training budget leads to monotonically decreasing performance. Abstract: Reliable uncertainty quantification remains an important challenge in AI. Hierarchical Bayesian methods provide a principled framework for this by representing unknown quantities through posterior distributions. Joint inference of neural-network parameters and prior hyperparameters is challenging for conventional Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods due to strong dependencies. In this work, we introduce the multilevel particle marginal Metropolis-Hastings (MLPMMH) method, which combines pseudo-marginal inference for the hyperparameters with coupled sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) across hierarchy of network-width truncations for conditional parameter inference. Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has substantially improved the reasoning of autoregressive and discrete-diffusion language models. Language models that generate continuous token embeddings are emerging as a strong alternative, but RL post-training for them remains understudied. We propose \method{}, a post-training framework for continuous flow language models. Such a model denoises token embeddings over multiple steps and decodes them into discrete tokens only at the last step. To obtain pathwise gradients, which backpropagate through continuous actions and have much lower variance than REINFORCE, we introduce a critic that estimates the value of intermediate token embeddings, bypassing the non-differentiable decoding step. Abstract: Voice agents built on large language models (LLMs) now handle customer calls, but in regulated applications completing the task is not enough: the agent must follow a conversational flow set by law. In debt collection, it must confirm it is speaking to the debtor before mentioning the debt, identify itself and the creditor, state the amount, and avoid prohibited language. Every creditor turns these rules into its own procedure and revises it. We ask whether a small, self-hosted policy can be trained once and then follow regulated procedures it has never seen. One machine-readable specification per deployment, FlowSpec, generates the policy instruction, gates the tools, supplies the supervision and defines the tests; the agent speaks only approved catalogue sentences. Abstract: Abstractive summarization remains challenging across languages, where linguistic quality and factual consistency may diverge, particularly in low-resource settings. We present a standardized zero-shot benchmark of eight closed-source and open-weight LLMs on size-matched English and Bengali XL-Sum test sets. Our evaluation combines lexical and semantic metrics with reference-free factuality verification and multidimensional LLM-as-a-Judge assessment, providing a comprehensive analysis of both surface-level quality and factual reliability in multilingual summarization. articles.title: Can LLMs Access their World Knowledge for Event Prediction?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19021v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent work has questioned whether large language models (LLMs) can be useful for temporal event prediction. Despite vast pretrained world knowledge, LLMs often underperform simpler specialized models. We ask whether this knowledge is truly inaccessible, or whether current methods fail to present event prediction in a form LLMs can use. We argue for the latter and show that LLMs become effective event forecasters when the interface is designed around two choices. The first grounds each event in a natural-language description, and the second separates event semantics from the prediction space to prevent semantic bias from label associations. To test this, we introduce DescribeEvent, a benchmark of ~150K events across seven datasets and six domains with event-level descriptions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19026v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse attention reduces the KV-cache traffic that dominates long-context LLM decoding, but practical methods largely operate at coarse granularity. Token-level selection offers finer control, yet presents two challenges: low-dimensional scoring may lose query--key structure needed for accurate ranking, while gathering scattered selected tokens can offset the resulting latency benefit. We introduce Joint Subspace Sparse Attention (JSSA) to address both challenges. For selection quality, JSSA learns a shared low-dimensional query--key subspace by minimizing token-score preservation error. We upper-bound the resulting non-convex objective with a tractable marginal objective that admits a closed-form spectral solution; direct refinement of the exact objective provides no measurable improvement in the tested settings. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19028v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Science fiction is widely credited with unsettling gender. This article asks whether that holds at the linguistic level, in how readily gendered reference gives way to its counterpart, a neutral term, or other social category, and whether it separates the genre from general fiction. It does so by masking man/men, woman/women, and person/people across same-period science fiction and general fiction corpora and classifying RoBERTa's five likeliest substitutes by gender. Retention and displacement are permutation-tested over five resampling rounds, and the underlying sentences are read closely. Both corpora cross the gender binary in both directions, but unequally: where woman is masked, the model predicts a masculine term about twice as often as it predicts a feminine term where man is masked. Abstract: Record linkage and demographic inference from names are routine demands in social science. Most approaches to these problems require labeled training data that are difficult or costly to acquire. I show that pre-trained language models perform both tasks accurately without requiring task-specific training. For record linkage, I introduce EnsembleLink, an algorithm that uses pre-trained embeddings alongside string-based scorers to retrieve a short list of candidates and then identify the likeliest matches. EnsembleLink matches or exceeds the performance of most prior approaches while generalizing across scripts and formats that those methods are unable to handle. For ethnicity inference from names, I show that large language models (LLMs) achieve up to 83.8% accuracy on U.S. voter files, compared to 78.0% for name-supplemented BISG. Abstract: Chatbot Arena ranks language models with the Bradley-Terry model, which gives each model one score and so assumes Luce's choice axiom. Choice theory predicts where this fails: near-copies are told apart more decisively than their scores imply. On 1.8 million Arena votes, votes between versions of one model are 1.37 times as decisive as Bradley-Terry predicts, between sizes of one generation 1.26 times and between models of one lab 1.12 times; a release a year later gives consistent multipliers, and the effect survives alternative tie treatments, prompt subsets and topics, and timing checks. How alike two models' answers are worded and formatted tracks the effect. articles.content:

Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) allows language models to adapt their behavior from instructions and demonstrations in a prompt, but accuracy alone does not reveal how contextual information controls their predictions. We study the acquisition and trainability of ICL with a controlled diagnostic that separates copying a nearby demonstration from integrating information across the prompt. Across 17 models, about a third prefer the copied answer, a few are undecided, and the rest prefer the rule-consistent answer, which goes with higher accuracy and with control by the requested value rather than the closest conflicting example. Checkpoint analyses show that models begin prioritizing task-relevant prompt tokens over conflicting examples long before their accuracy improves beyond chance level. articles.title: DecisionRobust: Benchmarking Robustness for JEV Style Decision Models Across Text and Vision
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19118v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Emerging decision models such as JEV provide typed interfaces that map task instructions and observations directly to choices, judgments, and scores. As these models are increasingly used for automated decision-making, understanding their reliability under adversarial manipulation becomes critical. We introduce DecisionRobust, a benchmark for systematically evaluating the robustness of decision models across textual and visual inputs. Our benchmark covers practical decision-making scenarios and a diverse suite of attacks, including semantics-preserving text perturbations, image perturbations, and prompt injection in both modalities. We curate evaluation sets through external validity checks and cross-model candidate selection. We evaluate 30 model configurations on text tasks and 17 on vision tasks, including 24 and 12 held-out models, respectively, that are excluded from candidate selection. Our experiments reveal several key findings.

articles.title: CAFE: Confining Feature Distillation to Language-Routed Adapters for Compact Multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19134v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Feature distillation is usually expected to add to logit distillation. We find that this expectation does not hold for two common feature losses in compact multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR), and analyze why through their gradients. The gradient of a projection-based loss is orthogonal to the task gradient, while that of Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA), a similarity-based loss, is weakly aligned with it. CKA lowers the word error rate (WER) on non-English languages, but at the expense of data-rich English. Three loss-level remedies (one trained, two probed) all fall short, and the CKA gradient overlaps with the subspace English uses in the shared encoder by 97.5% to 99.5% (about 81% by chance). Guided by this diagnosis, we propose CAFE (Confined-Adapter Feature distillation), which confines the CKA gradient to adapters that English bypasses, addressing the trade-off in the parameters rather than in the loss. Abstract: Mixed methods research offers established strategies for integrating qualitative and quantitative evidence, but less guidance for integrating two computational representations of the same qualitative corpus. This methodological study introduces Parallel-Then-Integrated (PTI), a four-step procedure for explicit and traceable integration. We present PTI using 1,203 interview paragraphs from 29 mothers in Nepal. The two representations were ontology-guided Patient Voice (PV) coding with PVminer and data-driven themes generated through non-negative matrix factorization (NMF). A theme-complete crosswalk documented convergence, divergence, and preprocessing-sensitive differences. Abstract: Meta-evaluation of text generation metrics and LLM-judges is primarily conducted using metric-human correlations. However, prior work has shown that correlation is not an appropriate estimate of a metric's evaluation capability and can be unstable across evaluation settings, such as different datasets or languages. Therefore, we propose a regression-based meta-evaluation of metrics that learns on calibrated metric outputs to predict human ratings. We ground this measurement relative to a trivial constant-mean baseline and human agreements to provide a comparable measure of metric capability across evaluation settings. To test our meta-evaluation framework, we developed a large-scale multi-lingual style-personalized text generation (SPTG) benchmark, collecting multiple annotations across 10 topologically diverse languages and four evaluation dimensions, each with varying degrees of subjectivity. Abstract: Harness optimization improves LLMs by refining reusable prompts and scaffolding, yet requires further adaptation for program generation tasks such as text-to-SQL and text-to-Python. Existing methods often rely on LLM reflectors to propose harness updates, which can fix observed failures but also disrupt previously correct behavior. Text-to-code tasks offer a natural way to mitigate this issue: we can execute generated outputs, allowing us to evaluate and verify the effects of proposed updates directly. Building on this signal, we introduce \textsc{HERO} (\textbf{H}arnessing \textbf{E}vidence for \textbf{R}efinement and \textbf{O}ptimization), which combines offline and test-time harness optimization. At the first stage, \method{} learns reusable prompt updates from execution-verified successes and failures and validates candidate revisions before adoption. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19185v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluation of large language models (LLMs) remains largely pre-scientific: it involves many design decisions, with little guidance on how to make them. These choices can substantially affect measured performance and, consequently, decisions about subsequent pretraining. To identify effective evaluation setups, we investigate 8 aspects, such as task formulation or the number of in-context examples. We compare the setups using three widely-used signal criteria, repurposed as normative meta-measures: monotonicity, non-randomness, and ranking consistency of the evaluation scores across intermediate checkpoints. In an early pretraining scenario, we evaluate these setups on 26 monolingual 2B-parameter models trained on different types of data, using 80 tasks in four languages. Abstract: Rare but severe failures of large language models can become practically significant at deployment scale. Estimating their probabilities with direct Monte Carlo sampling is highly inefficient, while proposal-based methods typically require auxiliary learning of an additional proposal distribution. We introduce \textbf{Weighted Ensemble (WE)}, a training-free framework for rare-event estimation in language models. WE samples exclusively from the original language model and improves upon direct Monte Carlo by periodically reallocating the sampling budget toward prefixes that appear more likely to reach the target rare event. Abstract: While work on LLM-based regression has largely focused on scalar prediction, multi-output text regression remains less explored. We present DualView, a parameter-efficient approach to leverage LLMs for multi-output text regression. \method{} first extracts broad and output-specific representations from a frozen LLM, then uses a dual-branch architecture to produce the full score vector. Across five heterogeneous regression tasks and eight LLMs (up to 122B), DualView outperforms seven supervised regression baselines while requiring 82--1842 times fewer fitted parameters than the three strongest baselines. These improvements extend across individual output dimensions and persist even with limited training data. Abstract: Transformers are efficient to pre-train at scale because attention permits parallel computation across sequence positions, but long-context inference requires increasingly large KV caches. Efficient recurrent alternatives reduce the asymptotic complexity of inference, but their sequential dependence limits token-wise parallelism during training, making them harder to scale. Further, the current paradigm of extending long context tasks creates competing notions of retaining information precisely and keeping long-context inference efficient. To address this gap, we introduce Titan-Llama, a post-training method for retrofitting attention-based language models with a hierarchical memory architecture that updates parameters at test-time. articles.title: Do Syntax Heads Influence Model Behavior?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19231v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transformer language models develop attention heads that specialize in syntactic relations, for example, attending from verbs to their subjects. Do these heads play a causal role in the model's syntactic predictions? Evidence for such a role is mixed to negative: even when we force these heads to attend to a distractor noun other than the subject, the model's syntactic predictions are still more consistent with the subject than with the distractor. Interventions on specialized syntax heads had a significantly stronger effect on syntactic predictions than interventions on random heads, but only in one of the two measures we propose.

articles.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transformers are intuitively considered to be efficient at copying from their inputs. We actually show that the ability of LLMs to copy in context can be improved through explicit modeling. We propose Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs), which add a lightweight Copy-Paste head to the conventional language modeling (LM) head. CPLMs improve training efficiency, downstream performance, and offer new operating points in long-context and retrieval setups. We validate our approach by pretraining models from 135M to 1.7B parameters, showing improvements across all scales and backbones with negligible training and inference overheads. We explain the success of CPLMs by showing that they partially mitigate the LM head gradient bottleneck through an alternative gradient path.

articles.title: Action Jets: Learning the Local Shape of the Action-conditioned Data Manifold
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19007v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: World models are a powerful means of reasoning and planning, but many of these action-conditioned predictive models are high dimensional and computationally expensive. These challenges limit the number of action candidates that can be evaluated by a planner. We show that this cost is avoidable for planners over short horizons, which only require local information with respect to the current state. For a fixed state, the frames reachable by varying a low-dimensional action (a camera movement or an end-effector command) lie on a low-dimensional manifold. Abstract: Modern image generation largely relies on specialized generative models that leave the process of image construction implicit in learned parameters. Abstract: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. arXiv:2610.19063v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As video models enable longer and more realistic interactive experiences, maintaining a world consistent with its history becomes essential. This requires both preserving previously observed content and ensuring coherent world evolution over time. World memory is a critical capability to evaluate alongside visual fidelity and video duration. We introduce WorldMemBench, a benchmark for systematically evaluating world memory in video world models. Across 260 test cases, it assesses static memory through the retention of human identity and appearance, object appearance and geometry, and environmental content and geometry, and dynamic memory through event progression and state persistence. Abstract: Monocular 3D object detection methods increasingly rely on depth-guided transformers, but they operate entirely in the perspective image plane where spatial relationships are distorted by foreshortening. We propose MonoMIP, a dual-decoder framework that adds complementary 3D geometric reasoning through Bird's-Eye View (BEV) features constructed via Multi-Height Inverse Perspective Mapping. We perform IPM at K elevation planes spanning ground to rooftop, producing an ordered stack of height-conditioned metric BEV features that reduces above-ground misprojection and exposes depth-dependent appearance variation across planes. A BEV decoder with multi-scale deformable attention aggregates this multi-height evidence per query, while a depth-guided 3D decoder provides complementary perspective-space predictions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19108v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have been widely applied in embodied agents and robotics for vision tasks. However, MLLMs suffer from limitations in spatial reasoning and perception. Post-training techniques have shown promise for improving these capabilities; yet, there are limited data-driven surveys of such approaches. In this survey, we consider approaches to fine-tuning pretrained MLLMs for spatial reasoning tasks, ranging from supervised to reinforcement learning, with an emphasis on the datasets used. We investigate themes of dataset construction, data modality and annotation, and evaluation of the resulting models. Abstract: Field pea has gained interest in the Midwest U.S. and has the potential to benefit Iowa cropping systems. This study evaluated 17 accessions and 7 Canadian varieties for agronomic and seed yield performance. This study found that PI accession trials exhibit genetic diversity in phenology and canopy traits, whereas the Canadian elite varieties demonstrated great yield potential under Iowa conditions. The accession genotypes matured between 75 DAP (late June) and 95 DAP (late July) across six site-years. The top-yielding Canadian varieties averaged 1961 kg/ha across two site-years. Abstract: We present LidarVerse, a real-time unified LiDAR world model for sensor simulation across tasks and sensors. Existing LiDAR simulators largely follow one of two complementary paradigms: reconstruction-based methods preserve the geometry of a captured scene but require lengthy per-scene optimization, whereas generative methods amortize learning across data but lack the consistency needed for long-horizon rollouts. LidarVerse brings both paradigms into a single, unified conditional generative framework. A universal tokenizer maps LiDAR range sequences into a shared latent space, where a bidirectional teacher learns a common interface for conditioning on a LiDAR prefix, an HD-Map, a persistent spatial cache, and optionally, text. Abstract: World models of visual information predict future image frames conditioned on given action sequences. This predicted scene evolution is driven by deterministic changes such as controlled motion on a robot platform, as well as stochastic changes such as rendering of manipulated objects or previously occluded regions. Our key insight is that the spatial location of these stochastic changes is itself learnable. We leverage this insight by jointly regressing both the deterministic next-state prediction and the spatial uncertainty map, then using the uncertainty map to guide a conditional diffusion process. We propose Decoupled Drift-Diffusion World Model (D3WM), which uses a transformer trained with a Gaussian negative-log-likelihood objective to produce both the deterministic next-state prediction and a spatial map of heteroscedastic aleatoric uncertainty. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19218v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Myopic vision degrades the quality of human vision due to spherical eye defocus aberrations that impair the perception of fine spatial details. To address this limitation, this work proposes a deep learning-based approach to computationally design transformed images that allow individuals with myopia in fixed distance to perceive scenes with enhanced clarity. The method trains a neural network to counteract defocus aberrations modeled using the second-order Zernike polynomial $Z_2^0$. The approach employs a U-Net architecture trained with a loss function combining reconstruction error minimization with spatial difference structural preservation through $\ell_1$ regularization. Training is carried out exclusively on the KITTI dataset, while testing is performed on DIV2K and ImageNet datasets, demonstrating generalization across diverse image distributions. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19257v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Memory for long-horizon video generation must satisfy two competing requirements: it must remain bounded so generation can continue indefinitely, while still recovering what was observed at a place when the camera returns, regardless of how long ago it was seen. Reconstruction-based memories provide spatial recall by caching and reprojecting explicit geometry, but require growing storage and depend on estimated 3D structure. Recurrent memories keep a constant-size state, but retention is governed by temporal recurrence, causing old observations to fade with time. We introduce SMART, a slot memory addressed by region tokens, which combines bounded storage with spatially addressed recall. Abstract: Existing illumination estimation methods primarily recover lighting distributions for rendering, but typically leave the contributions of individual physical light sources at specific scene locations implicit. We introduce LAMP, a framework for point-conditioned, source-aware illumination reasoning from a single RGB image with marked query points. LAMP constructs a shared inventory of active light sources, ranks contributing sources for each query, and predicts their 3D query-to-source directions. articles.content:

Abstract: One-step diffusion distillation achieves strong performance on small datasets but remains insufficient for high-resolution or complex text-to-image settings. Extending to multistep distillation often requires training data, suffers from early-step degradation, inconsistent outputs across sampling budgets, and incurs high computational cost. We identify that these limitations stem from simultaneous training, where a single adapted network approximates multiple score functions of different student distributions at once, causing biased distribution matching and unstable optimization. Abstract: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. Existing approaches rely on robot-tracked poses and latent-space prediction, but do not directly generate the observations required for interactive control. Abstract: Reliable recognition of accessibility-critical objects (e.g., audible pedestrian signals, door-activation buttons, and handrails) is essential for assistive navigation technologies that support safe, independent mobility for blind and low-vision (BLV) users. Yet these categories are underrepresented in existing large-scale vision datasets, and the few datasets that include them suffer from limited class coverage, inconsistent annotations, and poor diversity. We introduce NavAble, a large-scale dataset spanning 11 accessibility-critical object classes, combining 41K curated open-source images with 8K newly collected, densely annotated real-world images. Abstract: Multimodal knowledge graphs (MMKGs) organize information across different modalities to support multimodal Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which aims to improve the performance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Abstract: Pedestrian tracking in video is important for applications such as surveillance and scene analysis, but it becomes more challenging in crowded scenarios with frequent occlusions and rapid motion. Abstract: Achieving human-like dexterous manipulation remains a central challenge in robotics. Abstract: Deep space missions increasingly require spacecraft capable of autonomously operating in environments with communication delays and bandwidth limitations. A key enabler of such autonomy is the ability to run learning-based algorithms directly onboard. Abstract: Learning a collective policy for state-based Cartesian manipulation across diverse robotic embodiments presents a fundamental challenge due to embodiment-dependent transition dynamics. To address this, we propose PACE, a two-stage collective learning framework that separates shared task-space intent from embodiment-dependent transition dynamics. Abstract: While Vision-Language-Action models have enabled impressive cross-task transfer in zero-shot settings, \emph{adaptation} methods are often necessary to achieve consistent performance on novel tasks. articles.title: FACT: A Multimodal Force-Action-Track Foundation Model for Human-to-Robot Dexterity
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19155v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative to costly robot data collection for dexterous manipulation, but most human datasets lack force measurements. Dexterous manipulation requires not only visual and proprioceptive understanding but also the ability to anticipate and regulate interaction forces. To scale force-aware human-robot co-training, we introduce EgoForce, a large-scale human tactile dataset capturing force-rich manipulation experience, and combine it with robot demonstrations for pretraining. We present FACT, a robot foundation model that cascades from prospective visual planning to force-aware refinement for dexterous manipulation. FACT comprises two jointly trained components. A Track-Guided Coarse Planner jointly predicts actions, future video, and visual tracks. Future video and visual tracks also provide a shared task representation that facilitates cross-embodiment knowledge transfer and coarse action generation.

Abstract: Existing biomimetic lower-limb prosthesis controllers are commonly designed for discrete locomotion modes, requiring separate parameterizations for level walking, ramps, and stairs. Abstract: Reduced-order models (ROMs) make model predictive control (MPC) of high-dimensional nonlinear systems tractable, but the resulting modeling error can lead to constraint violations on the real system. We introduce CoRE-MPC, a robust MPC formulation that plans with a nonlinear ROM and guarantees recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction for the full-order system. articles.content:

Abstract: Robots following persistent language instructions must decide which cached room judgments remain valid as their environment changes. We present MIND (Maintenance via INstruction-conditioned Dependencies), a framework for maintaining target-room decisions without re-evaluating every room after each event. A language model compiles each instruction into dependencies for semantic qualification and target selection. Abstract: We present Keypoint Constraint Learning (KCL), a framework for learning task-relevant motion constraints from visual demonstrations and for planning safely with the extracted constraints. To make constraint learning tractable from RGB-D observations, we represent demonstrations using sparse 3D object-centric keypoints and semantic mask centroids extracted through segmentation, visual feature clustering, and point tracking. articles.title: Probabilistic Physics Digital Twin for Human-Robot Interaction
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19336v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Digital twins are increasingly used in robotics to simulate interactions, predict action outcomes, and support planning. However, constructing accurate digital twins requires precise estimates of physical properties such as mass, friction, and center of mass, which are often difficult to obtain in real-world environments. We propose probabilistic digital twins, which represent uncertain physical properties as probability distributions rather than fixed values. By simulating actions across these distributions, the twin predicts a range of possible outcomes and their likelihoods. These probabilistic simulations can guide both human and robot actions by identifying actions that are effective despite physical uncertainty. We demonstrate this framework through human-robot interaction scenarios, including interfaces that communicate simulated outcomes to users and robot planning strategies that explicitly account for uncertainty.

articles.title: Can Learning to Answer Spatial Questions Improve Novel-View Generation?
articles.content: Generating novel views from limited observations requires preserving both the appearance and spatial structure of a scene. Although recent approaches exploit fine-grained geometric cues, they do not explicitly model high-level semantic and spatial properties such as object identity, attributes, and inter-object relationships. In this work, we investigate whether 3D language understanding can provide complementary supervision for novel-view generation. We introduce Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal model with a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture. Our model incorporates camera geometry into both VAE and ViT representations and leverages understanding features during generation through joint self-attention with a modality-aware attention masking strategy. Experiments demonstrate strong image quality and geometric consistency in novel-view generation, alongside competitive 3D language understanding. Further analysis shows that joint training improves cross-view correspondence in VAE representations and similarity in a 3D-aware feature space.

articles.title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are gaining attention in autonomous driving, inheriting commonsense priors from large language models (LLMs) and widening the navigation interface from a fixed command set to free-form natural-language instructions. However, this open-ended interface exposes a new vulnerability surface: an inattentive driver may issue instructions that are unsafe given the current scene, and a malicious user may issue dangerous ones on purpose. We present the first benchmark suite that evaluates navigation following and conflict awareness together, along with adversarial robustness. Existing VLAs fall short on both: SimLingo completes no language-instructed lane change in closed loop, and all models degrade sharply under conflicting signals. We propose SafeDriveVLA, the first driving VLA that (1) explicitly predicts a three-level navigation-compliance mode to decouple conflict reasoning from action generation, and (2) uses navigation-conditioned world model dreaming to inform this prediction. Unlike prior world models that roll out expert or planned actions, ours dreams of strictly following the navigation signal, showing when following is safe. SafeDriveVLA reaches 88.16 Driving Score (DS) and 68.64% Success Rate (SR) on Bench2Drive, lifts closed-loop language following by 49.3% and reduces collisions under unsafe instructions from 60 to 38 compared to the best SimLingo variant. Video demonstrations are available on our project page.

articles.title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
articles.content: Recent advances in robot learning have driven rapid progress in humanoid control, enabling increasingly agile behaviors in the real world. However, humanoid control networks are typically obtained through conventional training procedures, while comparatively little attention has been given to directly modeling the distribution of their learned weights and generating functional networks in weight space. In this work, we investigate whether high-performing humanoid control networks can be generatively modeled directly through their weights. We adopt a latent diffusion framework that couples a linear autoencoder with a Diffusion Transformer. The autoencoder compresses actor network parameters into a compact latent space, and the Diffusion Transformer models the distribution of these latents. Trained on networks collected from reinforcement learning for the Unitree G1 robot, our approach generates deployable networks that perform various motions in the real world, including walking, dancing, and spin kick. Beyond generation, we further study the learned weight space to better understand the structure captured by these humanoid control networks. We identify a structural principle in the first-layer weights that consistently reflects the robot's kinematic prior. Notably, this kinematic prior emerges under both Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Imitation Learning (IL) training, suggesting that it is not specific to a particular optimization process but may instead reflect common knowledge associated with humanoid embodiment. Together, these results demonstrate the feasibility of generative modeling in humanoid network weight space, while providing initial insights into the information encoded by their learned weights. Additional results are available on our project website: https://humanoid-weight-diffusion.github.io/

articles.title: Representation Conditioning for Generation
articles.content: Representation-alignment methods effectively accelerate the diffusion transformer training. REPA, for example, uses a pretrained vision encoder to supervise an intermediate layer through an MLP projection head which is discarded after training. It aims to import semantics from the vision encoder to the diffusion backbone. While this objective is achieved at early layers by back-propagating the alignment loss, there is no guarantee that later layers, supervised by the velocity prediction loss alone, can well access such semantics. We propose a simple solution, representation conditioning (RECON), to improve semantics in later layers. During training, we feed the pretrained vision encoder tokens into later layers; during inference, because we no longer have the clean image, we reuse the MLP head (as a proxy to the vision encoder) and project its output tokens to the later layers. Our method adds no parameters and leads to much faster convergence: RECON is $63\times$ faster than SiT and $25\times$ faster than REPA. Code is available at https://github.com/saeidrazavi/RECON

articles.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
articles.content: Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) is a cornerstone of autonomous robotic systems, yet real-world fine-tuning remains a formidable challenge because of high-dimensional action spaces and intricate coupling between heterogeneous modules. In this paper, we propose HiRe-MoMa (Hierarchical Residual Mobile Manipulation), a systematic framework for stable and sample-efficient real-world fine-tuning of complex MoMa systems. At its core, HiRe-MoMa adopts a Hierarchical Residual Architecture that fine-tunes a frozen base policy. A Policy-Agnostic Residual learns additive corrections atop the base policy, while Hierarchical Decoupling splits the residual into mobile-base and manipulator-arm heads with unidirectional conditioning, mitigating gradient interference and aligning corrections with the platform's physical hierarchy. To improve sample efficiency in data-expensive real-world settings, we propose Expert-Guided Value Alignment, which leverages sparse human interventions with under 20% training coverage to reshape the critic's value landscape, effectively guiding autonomous exploration through expert priors. Extensive real-world experiments on the TIAGo++ platform demonstrate that HiRe-MoMa consistently enhances task performance with only around 30 minutes of online interaction, regardless of the base policy architecture. To our knowledge, this is among the first frameworks to enable efficient on-robot fine-tuning for mobile manipulation in the real world, providing a practical paradigm for deploying complex robotic systems in dynamic, human-centric environments. Further details can be found on our project website: https://hire-moma.github.io/

articles.title: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action
articles.content: World-action models aim to turn visual anticipation into driving decisions, yet typically train action experts on trajectory representations defined independently of visual dynamics. This motivates deriving action targets directly from visual motion. We first examine a simpler setting in which trajectories are reconstructed from recorded future images. Even without the need for future prediction, reconstruction captures the dominant maneuver but leaves centimeter-scale errors. We therefore introduce VITAL (Vision-Induced Tokens for Action Learning), an action tokenizer that couples a visually derived motion scaffold with a compact residual encoding the trajectory error left by that scaffold. This representation makes visual motion the principal prediction target and gives small metric corrections a separate, normalized learning scale. Using flow matching, the action expert jointly predicts both components from the current image, ego state, and navigation command, without generating future images at inference. The same residual coordinates support bounded reinforcement post-training that refines execution while keeping the predicted visual scaffold fixed. With only one action denoising step, VITAL achieves 90.8 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, within 0.13 points of its ten-step score at 3.29x the end-to-end inference speed. Without retraining, it achieves 91.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest and 38.6 on navhard. Project page: https://worldbench.github.io/vital

articles.title: CommerceGen-Studio: An End-to-End Framework for Commercial-Grade Main-Image Generation
articles.content: We present CommerceGen-Studio, an end-to-end framework for generating commercial-grade main images for e-commerce Stock Keeping Units (SKUs). Our framework is organized along a three-stage pipeline of information extraction, semantic rewriting, and multi-condition generation: Prompt-Eval-Refine-Loop Agent (PERL-Agent) distills heterogeneous SKU metadata into concise selling-point text lists through an iterative closed loop of VLM and LLM roles scored by a reference-free rubric. Layout Thinker Optimization (LTO) aligns the rewriter with both caption and rendered-image quality via alternating domain-specific policy optimization. SKU-DiT, trained under Reinforce-Distill-Reinforce (RDR) progressive training, conditions jointly on the white-background product image, the trademark crop, and the structured layout to hold subject fidelity, trademark integrity, and character-level text accuracy together. The framework runs in production at a scale of millions of main images per day with a latency of a few seconds per image, which we believe makes it among the first systems of this kind to operate at commercial scale. We also release CommerceGen-Bench, a benchmark of hard cases collected from live traffic across all product categories. On it, our framework achieves the highest overall scores among the evaluated open-source baselines on both editing tracks, with and without prompt enhancement. It also matches much larger closed-source models, and beats several of them at Instruction Following and Product Integration - the two properties that determine whether an image can be published.

articles.title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning
articles.content: Achieving general spatial intelligence requires a unified understanding of both static 3D and dynamic 4D. However, we find that existing models struggle to excel at both: 3D post-training can weaken dynamic understanding, while 4D-specialized models often lack strong static 3D reasoning. Our analysis reveals that this spatial--dynamic interference is highly non-uniform across parameter groups, with the balance between static and dynamic capabilities particularly sensitive to changes in late-layer MLPs. To address this interference, we propose DynThinker, a unified framework for jointly strengthening static and dynamic spatial reasoning. Decoupled Exponential Moving Average (D-EMA) applies configurable group-wise averaging to constrain drift in interference-sensitive pretrained parameters while preserving flexibility for capability enhancement. Spatial-Dynamic Fusion (SDF) complements D-EMA by selectively integrating spatial and temporal priors from a dynamic geometry encoder into intermediate VLM representations under semantic guidance. Across ten metrics spanning nine static 3D and dynamic 4D benchmarks, DynThinker achieves the highest average score among all evaluated models. Notably, DynThinker achieves 56.0 on ReVSI, 67.2 on DSR-Bench, and 51.2 and 40.1 under the sample-wise and group-wise evaluation protocols of DSI-Bench, respectively, setting new state-of-the-art results among the compared open-source models across all four evaluations within a unified model.

articles.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
articles.content:
Training language agents is bottlenecked by the high cost of long-horizon rollouts, yet standard agentic reinforcement learning (RL) learns only from a terminal scalar reward, leaving the supervision in intermediate steps largely unused. Prior work exploits this supervision through value targets that estimate per-step success probabilities or observation targets that fit environment response. Both are hard to construct well: (1) value targets come from the same single scalar signal for each step in the trajectory, and (2) observation targets, such as web pages and terminal logs, are long and noisy and reach only one step ahead. We propose 
ame, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets. On successful on-policy trajectories, 
ame trains the policy backbone to generate the action sequences that follows each history. Each action is also supervised when forecast from the preceding histories, forming a temporal ensemble that the shared backbone absorbs during training, and this enables acting and forecasting to co-evolve. The policy still acts one step at a time at inference, with no overhead. Across five benchmarks (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, $τ^2$-bench, and AppWorld), 
ame (1) achieves stronger aggregate performance than GRPO and RL baselines with predictive auxiliary targets across simulated environments, while improving overall performance on both realistic applications; (2) delivers up to $1.9	imes$ and $2.0	imes$ higher sample efficiency than ECHO and GRPO, respectively, on ScienceWorld; and (3) achieves these gains with a single policy backbone, without additional models, separate pretraining, or inference overhead. The codebase is available at https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/CoPE.
