articles.title: CoWear: Towards Collaborative Wearable Inertial Localization with Multiple Smart Devices
articles.content: Consumer smart devices observe the same human motion from different body locations, yet existing inertial-localization benchmarks rarely provide synchronized heterogeneous wearables with device-specific motion ground truth. We present CoWear, a dataset and reference framework for collaborative inertial localization using a smartphone, smartwatch, and smart glasses. The dataset contains over 30 participants, over 300 walking sessions, and more than 30 hours and 100 km of aggregate device trajectories, with each device individually tracked by motion capture. To enable collaboration across distinct body motions, we train role-specific estimators to predict the displacement of a common reference device over synchronized temporal windows. Their predictions are transformed to the world frame using gyroscope integration and fused according to learned uncertainty. Experiments using phone, glasses, and watch as reference targets show that multi-device fusion consistently improves both displacement and trajectory rollout accuracy over individual-device estimation. CoWear provides a dataset and reproducible baseline for studying collaborative inertial localization across heterogeneous consumer wearables.

articles.title: GeoThinker-$F$: Endogenous Predictive World Representations for Fast Spatial Intelligence
articles.content: Existing geometry-aware Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly rely on external 3D encoders to provide structural priors, but executing these additional encoder paths at inference introduces substantial latency and computational overhead. We propose GeoThinker-$F$, an efficient framework that internalizes spatiotemporal perception by transforming causal MLLM hidden states into predictive latent world representations. Our key insight is that intermediate semantic representations contain sufficient information to predict useful representations of current geometry and future semantics, without requiring an exact reproduction of features from a dedicated 3D encoder. To realize this idea, GeoThinker-$F$ adopts a decoupled two-stage training strategy. In the first stage, the MLLM backbone is frozen while lightweight Latent Frame Prediction (LFP) heads learn from an offline 3D geometry expert and next-frame semantic targets. In the second stage, the external expert is removed, and the model is jointly optimized to generate and selectively integrate its self-predicted priors through a specialized Spatial-Grounded Temporal (SGT) Fusion module. Extensive evaluations show that GeoThinker-$F$ eliminates runtime dependence on external 3D geometry encoders while maintaining competitive performance across diverse spatial intelligence benchmarks. It achieves up to a $3.6\times$ inference speedup, reducing latency from $1.45\,\mathrm{s}$ to $0.40\,\mathrm{s}$ while retaining strong spatial reasoning performance.

articles.title: Feed-Forward Multi-View Feature Coding for 3D Gaussian Splatting
articles.content: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods enable efficient reconstruction of 3D scenes from sparse multi-view images in a single forward pass, without scene-specific optimization. However, existing feed-forward scene-coding pipelines first generate a complete Gaussian representation and then encode its geometry and appearance attributes separately, often involving non-differentiable operations. The resulting 'generate-then-compress' pipeline requires complex attribute-specific codec designs and limits rate-distortion performance by restricting the exploitation of cross-attribute redundancy. We propose multi-view feature coding for Gaussian splatting (MFGS), an end-to-end feed-forward framework for scene coding. Instead of compressing an explicit Gaussian representation, MFGS extracts multi-view features from the input images and encodes them into a compact bitstream. Through end-to-end rate-distortion training, MFGS learns compact multi-view features that jointly represent geometry and appearance, enabling the receiver to predict Gaussian attributes from the decoded features. We further introduce importance-guided Gaussian selection to accommodate different rendering budgets, allowing the receiver to adjust the number of Gaussians used for rendering from the same bitstream. Across RE10K, ACID, and DL3DV, MFGS achieves 99.76-99.86% bitrate savings over the generate-then-compress pipeline, as measured by BD-rate, while reducing total GMACs by 52-55% and providing an approximately 12 times end-to-end speedup.

articles.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
articles.content: Scaling up transformers has produced models with broad capabilities, deployed across heterogeneous hardware and fluctuating workloads. Yet, model families offer only a few fixed sizes (e.g., S, B, L), forcing users to commit to a model based on hardware and latency constraints. This rigidity is often suboptimal under varying query loads. We introduce a retraining-free method that elastifies pre-trained transformers into a single model that adapts on-the-fly across a continuum of computational budgets. Our key contribution is a differentiable relaxation of the functional unit-ranking problem: unlike prior work, which optimizes a single importance weight per MLP block or attention head, we rank every individual MLP neuron and attention head jointly, on a common scale, by minimizing the model's loss under soft pruning across many sparsity targets, all at once. Across 27 vision and text transformer encoders ranging from 22M to 8B parameters, our method yields smooth degradation up to 60% sparsity and outperforms one-shot baselines under deep pruning. For example, pruning DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 to 50% sparsity removes 427M parameters while reducing ImageNet-1k linear-probing accuracy by only 0.8%, without the need for weight correction or retraining. At 60% sparsity, a pruned AugReg ViT-B/16 model achieves up to $1.80\times$ higher throughput and $1.26\times$ lower single-query latency on an A100 GPU. Elastic models are produced in minutes, with construction time scaling sub-linearly with parameter count.

articles.title: Price of Anarchy of First-Price Auctions in Agentic Markets
articles.content: An agentic market is a decentralized serving-time market where AI agents bid to claim each user prompt. An agent's bid is based on its expected value for the prompt, which is the expectation of the reward for its response minus its inference costs. First-price auctions (FPAs), in which the highest bidder pays its bid and receives the prompt, are a natural way to allocate prompts in such a market, since they are simple and transparent to run, and do not require central knowledge of private capabilities and costs. However, FPAs are not truthful: participants may bid less than their true value in the hope of a larger profit, and the prompt may then be allocated to someone other than the bidder who values it the most. This welfare loss is quantified by the $\textit{price-of-anarchy}$ (PoA). In this paper, we argue that agentic markets are likely to possess features that reduce the price-of-anarchy. The first is a $\textit{competitive floor}$, which occurs when multiple bidders usually value the prompt above some baseline share of the optimal welfare (e.g., because the best models are often distilled into cheaper alternatives, which perform similarly). We show that competition among them then limits the welfare loss, which can be driven to zero as the floor rises. The second feature is $\textit{near-independence}$ of values after conditioning on the prompt, which occurs when most of the predictable variation in the expected value is determined by the difficulty of the prompt. As the value distribution approaches conditional independence, we can derive an efficiency guarantee that approaches a factor of $1 - 1/e^2$ of the optimal welfare. Thus, both features give rise to welfare lower bounds that are significantly better than the well-known general case of $1 - 1/e$. We validate these results empirically using auctions with strategic bidders simulated on the EmbedLLM prompt routing dataset.

articles.title: Continuum Attention
articles.content: We introduce Continuum Attention (CA), a causal Transformer attention operator that replaces discrete key and value lookup with integration over a continuous, piecewise linear memory curve. Each query induces an exponential relevance density along the curve. Integrating the density and interpolated values yields exact normalized attention from closed form exponential moments, including half token boundary contributions. The gradients follow analytically from moments of order at most two, enabling parallel GPU implementations while retaining quadratic sequence complexity and the standard Transformer decoder. Compared with ordinary softmax and focal attention, CA reduces mean validation negative log likelihood by 0.0200 and 0.0480 nats per byte, respectively, winning all paired comparisons. An additional disjoint validation slice yields a 0.0457 nats per byte advantage over the strongest selected softmax baseline, with a paired 95% confidence interval. These findings motivate continuous integration as a promising attention alternative while leaving larger scale generalization open.

articles.title: Learnable Hodge-Laplacian Driven Mixture of Experts for Steady-PDE Surrogates on Coarse Unstructured Meshes
articles.content: Current approaches for steady partial differential equations surrogate models on unstructured meshes apply a single mixing mechanism to the whole solution. This paper proposes an architecture that partitions the solution among vanilla transformer experts, each focused on a different spectral scale. The partition is built from a discrete Hodge Laplacian $L_0=\star_0^{-1} d_0^{\top}\star_1 d_0$, that serves as a fitting layer measuring high-frequency content. A gating mechanism takes the mesh as input and produces the per-vertex weights that recombine the expert outputs. AirFRANS is a steady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) airfoil benchmark. We evaluate our approach in a reduced remeshed version of the benchmark with each unstructured mesh counting 9.6K faces and 4.9K vertices. We compare our approach with the Transolver on the same dataset and dataset slit. Our approach reduces relative $L_2$ error by 31\% and interior mean squared error by 47\%.

articles.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
articles.content: Computer-use agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in interpreting screens and executing keyboard and mouse actions. However, games, with their visually rich worlds and diverse mechanics, remain challenging and offer a demanding next step toward general digital control. Current game-agent learning pipelines often rely on large-scale demonstrations with limited coverage of dynamic game states, while scalable environments for interactive training remain difficult to obtain. We introduce Player-1, a post-training framework for learning game control beyond demonstrations through synthetic experience. We extend the computer-use action space with relative pointer motion, sustained inputs, and composite actions. For supervised initialization, we fine-tune computer-use models on 6,044 curated gameplay trajectories that pair recorded actions with task instructions and visual reasoning. We construct Player-1-Gym, sixteen synthetic 2D and 3D environments designed around control demands shared across games. Programmatically verifiable rewards and randomized observations and control dynamics support multi-environment reinforcement learning with PPO. The resulting Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B improve MineDojo-300 success over their SFT policies by 27.8 and 17.7 percentage points, respectively. Player-1-9B reaches 38.33% success compared with 12.63% for the strongest evaluated baseline, with further gains over SFT on ViZDoom-10 and GameWorld. Further analyses show that broader synthetic environment coverage improves transfer, while the use of composite actions that combine multiple keyboard and mouse inputs increases during RL. We demonstrate that learning from synthetic experience substantially improves game control beyond supervised initialization, with gains that generalize beyond the RL training suite.

articles.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
articles.content: Long contexts enlarge key--value (KV) caches, increasing memory use and attention costs during generation. Compressing these caches must preserve information for unseen questions. We introduce **Latent Compaction**, which learns a compact document-specific cache through test-time training. We initialize cache entries using reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity. Training first fits attention outputs and log-normalizers to those of the full cache, with reconstruction-selected entries held fixed. It then jointly optimizes the entire cache through end-to-end distillation from the full-cache model. Model weights remain frozen throughout, and training uses only generic prompts about the document, without access to downstream questions or answers. Experiments on RULER, LongBench, and Phonebook Lookup demonstrate substantial gains over budget-matched compression baselines. On a RULER, for example, our method achieves 96.7% accuracy at 32$\times$ compression, compared with 40.0% for KVZip+. The method also transfers across model scales and families, with retrieval gains on both Qwen3 and MiniCPM5. These results show that treating the KV cache as a neural network and optimizing it with test-time training can preserve retrieval accuracy under aggressive compression. The code is released at https://www.github.com/THUNLP/latent-compaction

articles.title: PingpongDuo: Agile Humanoid Table Tennis Doubles with Safe Team Coordination
articles.content: Unlike singles, humanoid table tennis doubles requires teammates to strike in strict alternation while sharing a confined workspace. Rapid repositioning can compromise striking accuracy, while uncoordinated teammate movements introduce collision risks. We present PingpongDuo, a hierarchical framework for agile humanoid doubles with safe team coordination. At the team level, a planner jointly selects positioning targets and uses learned risk estimates to filter risky proposals, preferentially preserving the current striker's target. At the individual level, separate footwork and striking skills combine agile movement with precise racket control. The skills are guided by human motion references, including footwork collected from human doubles play, and trained from states produced by one another to support rapid transitions. A racket-arm residual further refines strikes after movement using return feedback from a simulator calibrated with real ball-flight and contact measurements. In simulation, PingpongDuo improves the ball-return success rate by 13.2% over the state-of-the-art baseline, while achieving approximately 2 cm positioning error during clearance. In real-world experiments, a robot completes a 2.15 m clearance-and-recovery cycle in 2.4 s with a peak speed of 2.23 m/s, while two robots sustain more than 10 consecutive strikes in strict alternation.

articles.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
articles.content: Post-training binds the competence of an LLM agent to the interface it was trained on. Semantics-preserving perturbations of that interface, such as renaming an action or changing the notation, leave the underlying task unchanged yet make the agent worse at it. Scoring each sample independently means interface randomization only broadens this dependence from a single interface to the training interface distribution, so out-of-distribution perturbations still degrade the agent. We propose Cross-Interface Policy Regularization (CIPR), a self-supervised objective that replaces action names with uninformative identifiers and presents each training sample under two interfaces in which equivalent actions are identified by construction. CIPR penalizes the KL divergence between the action distributions induced under the two interfaces, so the policy behaves consistently across them. We evaluate CIPR in both supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training, where it improves robustness. On agentic function calling, held-out interface perturbations reduce the accuracy of a post-trained agent by nearly 25%, and CIPR recovers 10.5% while leaving accuracy on the unchanged interface intact.

articles.title: Beyond LLM Judge: Mechanical Verification for Agentic Autoformalization
articles.content: We introduce a novel method for verifying Lean formalizations that goes beyond LLM-judged faithfulness. Unlike most verification methods, which rely on LLMs or trained models, our method combines LLM-based semantic review with mechanical numerical and vacuity checks, providing checkable feedback and detecting errors missed by LLM judges. We apply this method, along with our Extract-Verify-Proof autoformalization pipeline, to construct the Formalized Library of Mathematical Functions (FLMF), a partial formalization of the NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions (DLMF). On three labeled datasets, our method achieves the lowest accepted-error rate among the evaluated methods, measured as the fraction of incorrect statements accepted by the verification method. Expert review of the results also identifies translation and source defects in existing datasets. Code available at https://github.com/annamei1/FLMF-Ch7ErrFunc-Release.git.

articles.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
articles.content: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student model on its own rollouts with token-level supervision from a teacher, assuming that the teacher can reach a correct answer from any prefix the student writes. We call this property the recoverability of the teacher and show it fails on incorrect rollouts: the teacher follows student errors, although it recognizes them. We propose CriticOPD, using error recognition to restore recoverability. The teacher critiques an incorrect rollout, allowing the student to rewrite its solution following the error. The resulting output, including the critique as privileged information, is scored by the teacher while the student uses the revision without the critique for training. On two Qwen3 students and six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, CriticOPD improves OPD, with the largest gains on competition problems.

articles.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
articles.content: Long-form agentic video generation must turn a screenplay into shots that remain spatially and temporally consistent across nonconsecutive requests. Passing prompts or recent frames between shots does not provide a shared spatial frame for revisiting a scene or a time-indexed record for replaying an earlier event. We present Any Time, Any Space (ATAS), which compiles a screenplay into shot requests with explicit location, camera, and event-time references. Before generation, it retrieves relevant evidence from a scene memory of registered static geometry and an event memory of dynamic observations indexed by scene, event, and time. After generation, ATAS reconstructs and registers the clip. It updates memory only when review and state checks accept the observation, while film delivery remains independent of memory admission. Across four video generators, ATAS improves all reported cross-shot consistency measures and achieves the highest aggregate benchmark score for each backbone. It also outperforms the compared agents and 3D-guided methods on target-image spatial revisit, leads three event-recapture criteria, and receives the highest human ratings on all six criteria. The video results and code are available on our project page: https://lhmd.top/atas/.

articles.title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2: Reproducible Safety Alignment for a Native Brazilian-Portuguese LLM. Negative DPO Results, a Controlled Composition Scan, and a Silent Failure Mode of the LLM Judge
articles.content: Brazilian Portuguese remains underserved by open-source language models, and the few that are safety-aligned rarely document what did not work or validate comparisons with statistical significance. We present Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, the second-generation post-training alignment of Manacá-1B (1.72B parameters, trained from scratch for PT-BR), with an SFT corpus of 291,223 examples. We document three DPO attempts, all negative, including a case where the training reward margin reaches 1.0 while free generation does not change at all, and show that safety came from a dedicated safety-SFT (LLM-jp AnswerCarefully style), refined over three iterations until closing the safety-helpfulness frontier. A controlled scan of the fraction of general data in the safety-SFT mix (10% to 60%) reveals a non-monotonic over-refusal curve with a knee point at 40-50%. The final model is compared against four external PT-BR models on the same items, with Wilson confidence intervals and paired McNemar tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction: the lower bound of its safety interval (94.1%) lies above the upper bound of all four baselines. We also report a methodological finding for LLM-judge evaluation: on two of six safety items in MT-Bench-PT, the judge categorically refuses to assign a score regardless of the evaluated response, silently reducing the effective N of that category in every prior report of the project. We complement this with an n-gram decontamination check and a Chinchilla-anchored compute-budget table that attributes the gap in general capability to pre-training scale rather than alignment methodology. All code, raw data, logs, and scripts that produce every reported number are publicly released.

articles.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
articles.content: Automated research with LLM agents has shown promising results in various domains. Through iterative refinement and scored verifiers, LLM agents are capable of discovering new ideas. There are different ways to scale automated research: let one agent iterate for longer, run several agents in parallel, or further let the parallel agents communicate and build on one another's candidates. However, we find that all three strategies eventually plateau as the agents accumulate history. Each agent becomes anchored to its own past attempts, making fewer and smaller edits. Beyond this point, additional budget brings little further improvement. In this paper, we show that the key to scaling discovery further is to forget. Periodically discarding the search state, including every agent's session and the candidate history, and restarting from the best candidate found so far, unblocks the search and pushes the same budget further.   We implement forgetting in a team of agents with communication and evaluate it on four tasks spanning heuristic programming, kernel optimization and model training. The results show up to 15% improvement compared to parallel agents, and up to 39% compared to a single agent. Our results suggest that, for open-ended discovery, what an agent is allowed to remember matters as much as how much compute it is given.

articles.title: A$^3$PreCore: Robust Rigid Registration for Native FLAIR-Space Brain-Mask Transfer
articles.content: Reliable brain-mask transfer into native fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) space can fail when T1-to-FLAIR rigid registration is unstable. We developed A$^3$PreCore, a six-degree-of-freedom rigid-registration strategy that aligns the full bias-corrected T1-weighted image to native FLAIR using normalized mutual information while preserving the established T1-space anatomical mask. We also introduced extended quantitative quality control (E-QC), which characterizes mask extent, field-of-view-relative position, FLAIR intensity support, boundary support, inferior morphology, and pairwise geometric disagreement. In 78 participants with paired T1-weighted and FLAIR imaging, A$^3$PreCore was compared with fsl_anat and the Brain Extraction Tool (BET). Gross rigid-body misregistration occurred in 21/78 fsl_anat outputs (26.9%) and 0/78 A$^3$PreCore outputs (exact two-sided McNemar p=9.54 x 10^-7). Among 57 participants without gross fsl_anat misregistration, A$^3$PreCore preserved close agreement (median Dice=0.993; median paired Delta NMI=-0.00007, p=0.429). A$^3$PreCore remained broadly concordant with BET (median Dice=0.955), with less inferior and extracranial extension in representative comparisons. Method-blinded neuroscientists ranked A$^3$PreCore first in 35/40 participants (87.5%). E-QC additionally exposed severe orientation-related disagreement not evident from global descriptors or centroid displacement alone. These findings support A$^3$PreCore as a robust native-FLAIR brain-mask transfer strategy and E-QC as a complementary framework for multidimensional mask characterization and participant-specific geometric quality control.

articles.title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
articles.content: 3D object composition is pivotal to digital content creation and robot simulation, while also serving as a critical testbed for physical intelligence in foundation models. Previous methods either leverage large language models to directly predict object coordinates, or utilize generative diffusion priors to synthesize composite images for visual alignment, both of which rely on static priors in digital spaces. However, these methods consistently struggle with complex compositions such as precise hanging, gravity-driven settling and hidden containment, as these tasks require interactive construction processes involving global planning, fine-grained alignment, and physical simulation. To address these challenges, we propose PhySGA, a Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for 3D composition via agent exploration and physical simulation, enabling the universal interactive assembly of rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Directly applying vanilla LLMs or VLMs to this task proves insufficient, as current models inherently lack grounded physical understanding and interactive construction experience. To overcome this limitation, we design a collaborative feedforward-feedback architecture: an Assembly Agent focuses on geometric and kinematic reasoning for global step planning and coarse adjustment, while a Critic Agent reasons over contact dynamics for simulator state diagnosis and fine-grained closed-loop correction. Furthermore, Action Routers map semantic planning and analysis onto executable physical primitives within the simulator, while a task-specific Self-Evolving Skill Library distills historical trial-and-error feedback into reusable experiences, boosting success rates and minimizing exploration attempts. Extensive experiments within Isaac Sim demonstrate that PhySGA significantly surpasses existing methods in relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.

articles.title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation
articles.content: Interactive video generation commonly relies on small bidirectional chunks to reduce response latency. Yet our preliminary experiments show that larger chunks improve video quality and better utilize GPU parallelism, allowing more latents to be sampled with only a modest increase in sampling time. Motivated by these observations, we propose Speculative Sampling, a strategy that combines the modeling power of large bidirectional windows with the low-latency interaction of small ones. It expands the modeling window by appending noise latents as padding and caches the resulting predictions for reuse when the condition remains unchanged. Predictions are delivered incrementally, while the uncommitted future remains replaceable. Our latency analysis shows that this removes the waiting-time lower bound imposed by chunk boundaries, shifting the optimization focus from reducing chunk size to accelerating per-chunk sampling. Bidirectional window size thus becomes a decision variable for jointly optimizing visual quality and sampling time, rather than a necessary constraint on low-latency interaction. This opens a path to serving large bidirectional models in interactive streaming systems without complex streaming post-training.

articles.title: KinoGen: Customizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation References via Kinematically Grounded Video Generation
articles.content: We present KinoGen, a framework that synthesizes customizable humanoid loco-manipulation references through kinematically grounded video generation. KinoGen conditions a pretrained video generator on calibrated renders of the target robot and object in a simulated task instance and recovers the reference by fitting the same models to the generated two-view video, so that the reference lies in the robot configuration space by construction without a human body proxy or retargeting. Body, hand, and object priors initialize the reconstruction, and direct optimization against cross-view evidence refines it. Since an edited keyframe is simply another rendered state, a user can prescribe a goal object pose, regenerate the video around the edited keyframe, and obtain a reference that satisfies the pose exactly. Across eight loco-manipulation tasks, KinoGen yields lower penetration and foot skating than video-based baselines and preserves over 90% of annotated contacts, and its customized references satisfy every prescribed target with substantially less penetration than direct interpolation. Tracking policies trained on the synthesized references are deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands. Project webpage: https://kinogen-humanoid.github.io/.

articles.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
articles.content: Understanding the social intelligence of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly important for applications involving human-AI interaction and multi-agent environments. Social intelligence comprises two aspects: cognitive intelligence, the ability to infer others' mental states, and behavioral intelligence, the ability to select appropriate social actions based on these inferences to achieve social goals. Persuasion provides a natural testbed in which both aspects are simultaneously at play, yet prior benchmarks typically evaluate them in isolation using synthetic scenarios. We introduce PerSo, a benchmark that evaluates both aspects on real-world persuasion dialogues from Reddit's ChangeMyView community, using an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline to construct the evaluation tasks, validated through human annotation. Our evaluation of diverse LLMs shows that performance generally scales with model size but varies across dimensions. The strongest LLM slightly surpasses the best observed human performance on the behavioral task, while the best human participant remains ahead on the cognitive task.

articles.title: AI 短剧日产 1500 部：一场全员狂飙下的 「无人生还」
articles.content: “现在整个短剧行业就是一片混乱，每个人都很焦虑、很迷茫。”这是过去一个月里，雷峰网与多位 AI 短剧从业者交流时，听到最多的一句话。上个月刚跑通的流程，这个月平台改了分账规则又得重新算账。好不容易摸清了提示词的写法，AI 视频生成工具一更新经验立马作废。甲方的尾款还没到账，下一部剧的制作成本已经垫出去了。这个行业节奏快到近乎疯狂，但没人说得清终点和方向。眼下，AI 短剧日上线量已突破 1500 部，制作成本从真人剧的几十上百万压缩到五万以内，大批团队仍在涌入赛道。可几乎所有受访者传递同一个信号：除了平台，几乎没人真正赚到钱。01 一部剧的生死，只有三天用传统内容生意的逻辑很难理解 AI 短剧，它更像一场高速运转的概率赌局。今年 8 月底，短剧编剧朱晓冉选择从大厂辞职。在真人短剧时代，编剧花一个月打磨本子是常态，但AI 短剧爆发后，她的工作节奏被彻底改写。“领导觉得有了 AI 工具，写本效率也该跟着上来。上半年最忙的时候，我一个月交了四个本子。剧本送交承制方后，几天就能产出成片。”产量快速拉高，质量却很快摸到了天花板。在朱晓冉看来，纯人工打磨的剧本可以做到九十分甚至一百分，AI 辅助创作的剧本上限大多只有八十分。“老板也很清楚这一点，但他更想要四个八十分，而不是一个一百分。” 朱晓冉表示。“这个行业现在本质是靠量赌概率，我们统计过 AI 短剧的爆率大概是千分之四，其余的基本都是无效产出。” 朱晓冉解释了一下这个逻辑，就算前面花六百万拍十部都扑了，只要第十一部赚了七百万覆盖全部亏损，这套商业模式就成立。“真人短剧粗制滥造一点三四十万就能拍出来，精品剧的制作费得一百万到一百五十万左右，但现在一部AI短剧的总投入五万就能搞定。”分成上，朱晓冉透露通常是编剧几千到一万，制作两三万到三四万，整个环节的总成本被压得极低。但产出剧集只是开始，拿到曝光才是整个环节的生死关口。“一部剧上线后，三天内没起量基本就凉了，不会有什么长尾效应。因为曝光最集中的时间就是前三天投流期，如果三天内起不来，大家就会立马放弃投流转投新剧。” 朱晓冉坦言。拥有九年影视从业经验的短剧导演瑾诺分享，短剧极度依赖投流，纯靠自然流量做火的案例业内确实也有，但概率几乎等于中大乐透。“投流这个环节大平台有专门的运营部门和投流手，外面也有专门的投流公司，好的投流手甚至能把一个一般的剧本投成大爆款。”但就算有投流加持，AI 短剧也会遭遇流量瓶颈。“某短剧平台的流量池有个别称叫‘流量黑盒子’，热度到 4000 万推你去下一层，5000 万再推。但 AI 漫剧到 4000 万就上不去了，开始卡流量。当然，推流机制没人知道，内部是否可以操控，无人知晓。” 瑾诺说。流量之外，收入也越来越少。目前在多数平台模式下，制作方收入主要分为两块：平台给剧本的保底金，以及剧集上线后的播放量分成。瑾诺坦言，“上半年国内 AI 短剧市场还能赚钱的，但现在不行了。因为很多短剧平台调整了分成规则，现在做 AI 漫剧可能横屏能小赚一点，但是整体要求也会相对应更高，不然自制基本亏本。”规则确实在变，今年4 月，红果率先下调AI 漫剧基础分账系数：AI 仿真人分账系数从 60 下调至 40，3D 漫剧从 50 下调至 40，同时取消中小团队 AI 仿真人剧本普惠保底。到了9月，红果又在《优质 AI 剧生产活动 2.0》中，取消了行业批量做 IP 续集赖以获利的系列剧规模系数。对靠批量做 IP 续集获利的团队来说，这条路也收窄了。“能拿到可观分成的只有金字塔尖极少数，大部分项目连成本都收不回来。” 朱晓冉补充。02 月薪三千的抽卡师，一周见真招的 AI 导演外界普遍认为AI降低了短剧行业的准入门槛，但在一线从业者视角，这反而是对从业者能力的重新洗牌。AI 介入生产短剧生产之后，催生了一个新岗位 —— 抽卡师。编剧只负责完成剧本，但AI视频生成工具读不懂剧本，需要有人把每一个镜头拆解成工具能理解的提示词描述，这就是抽卡师的工作。朱晓冉举了一个例子，“比如剧本写‘他看着对方’，抽卡师就要扩写成带表情、神态的详细描述，然后把这段描述喂给 AI 反复生成画面，直到抽出一个合格的镜头，视频生成环节真正做视觉细化的是抽卡师。”这是链条里不可或缺的一环，虽然用人量很大，但在行业内却属于"黑工"。“老板觉得没什么技术含量，就是把人话翻译给 AI 听，所以工资压得很低，但 KPI 又压得很重。这个岗位非常重要，但在现有模式下更像是很苦的纯力工。”朱晓冉表示。都是抽卡，但同一套AI生成工具，不同的人交出的结果完全天差地别。瑾诺认为，AI 就像一个加速器，把从业者的天赋、能力差距极度放大。“因为 AI 的考核更透明，有经验的人一个镜头两三次就能出，返工率高的人要七八次，这个成本差就会达到一倍以上。达

articles.title: 爱诗科技香港办公室正式开幕，落地数码港共建香港AI枢纽
articles.content: 香港，2026年10月13日——全球领先的AI视频大模型公司爱诗科技（AIsphere）今日宣布其香港办公室在香港数码港正式开幕。其香港办公室不仅是办公空间，更定位为辐射本地企业、政府机构、高校及创作者的AI枢纽。开幕当日香港办公室即投入运营，公司日后将招募更多本地员工并持续举办面向产业的专场活动，逐步建设汇聚创作者、高校与产业伙伴的「香港AI视频大本营」。爱诗科技联合创始人兼总裁谢旭璋及署理投资推广署署长刘智元、香港数码港行政总裁郑松岩博士、香港引进重点企业办公室副总监杨树源、香港生产力促进局主管等重要嘉宾出席剪彩仪式，与在港科技企业、金融投资机构、高校及社会各界代表共同见证爱诗科技落地香港。首度公布本地合作，启动「数智香港·爱诗AI百业共创计划」香港特区政府近日公布《施政报告》及首份五年规划（2026—2030年），明确提出以人工智能赋能千行百业、持续推进「人工智能+」行动，并加快算力基础设施建设、提升市民人工智能素养，为本地AI产业发展提供清晰指引。在此背景下，作为首批正式在港设立办公室的AI视频大模型公司，爱诗科技在开幕当日即宣布开启「数智香港·爱诗AI百业共创计划」，向香港各界发出合作邀请。谢旭璋在接受媒体采访时表示：「香港拥有国际化的视野、扎实的科研基础和活跃的创意产业，是我们全球发展的重要一站。作为港投公司科技生态圈的企业，我们希望成为连接香港各行业的AI枢纽。未来，我们将和香港本地高校共同举办AI视频模型相关的学术论坛，更希望与本地企业、青年与创作者一起，把AI视频和实时世界模型的能力真正用到产业和创作中去。」开幕当日，爱诗科技与在港科技企业、高等院校及青年社会团体签署多项战略合作文件，共同推动香港AI应用的落地与发展。在产业合作方面，公司与空间智能企业其域创新达成战略合作，融合真实世界三维重建与AI视频生成技术，围绕影视、文旅、地产等行业场景探索联合解决方案，携手开拓海外市场；在教育科研方面，公司与香港理工大学开展合作，将AI视频创作引入人文教学，结合中国历史与文化课程，探索负责任AI与数字叙事的教学实践，并在此基础上拓展人才培养、学生实习及联合研究等合作方向，推动产学研协同发展。此外，爱诗科技亦非常重视AI视频模型在社会服务方面的实际应用，推动技术真正走向普惠。公司当日宣布与香港福建三明联会青年委员会携手，未来将面向在港乡亲及青年开展AI科普讲座、创作体验工作坊及科技企业参访，并依托其闽港两地网络，联合开展「AI看三明」等两地青年交流与AI文化共创活动；同时，公司也与本地社团香港青年新创见展开合作，探索AI技术在社团建设、社区服务及青年交流中的应用，如在社区和学校开展AI讲座、运用AI视频制作防诈骗等公益内容，以及支持「一带一路」沿线青年交流活动。「系统化的科普展示和互动体验可提升大众对AI的理性认知，为技术应用营造更加包容、稳健的社会环境，夯实人工智能在香港长期发展的社会基础。」爱诗科技香港首席代表潘援介绍。PixVerse R2 现场亮相，多模型为香港各行业赋能今年以来，爱诗科技PixVerse R2在内的多个旗舰模型深度融入本地优势行业，更好地服务于香港数字内容产业与实体经济。在影视文创领域，香港拥有深厚的影视积淀和成熟的创作人才，PixVerse系列模型的电影级视觉、多镜头调度与角色一致性能力，可在前期开发阶段帮助创作者将剧本、人物与世界观转化为可讨论、可验证的影像，为分镜、动作、特效与风格探索提供新工具，助力香港电影工业拓展创作边界、培育青年创作者、推动香港故事走向国际市场。在文旅领域，实时世界模型可为景区、博物馆与文旅项目生成可交互的沉浸式导览与个性化体验内容，让香港的城市文化资源以更生动的方式触达全球游客。在广告营销与电商领域，品牌内容可依据用户反
